Develops FOSS tools and methods to effectively defend critical infrastructure using modern tech. Builds algorithms for sovereignty, understanding and long term sustainability.

Constanze is a physicist  (Albert Einstein Institute and Johns Hopkins) and left academia for a decade leading digital transformation initiatives in regulated sectors. Now, funds her research independently and partners with universities and research institutes. Founded fusioncore.ai and CNCG "Securitynative Europe"

speakers.name: Drew Bowman
speakers.title: EM AI SDLC @ Podiumc
speakers.bio: Drew Bowman has been building software and mentoring engineers for 20 years. He is a passionate about helping people and giving them tools to succeed. His core values are be generous and do hard things and applies those to his work and life.

speakers.name: Drew Brown
speakers.title: Developer Relations Engineer - Google Cloud
speakers.bio: Drew Brown is a Developer Relations Engineer (DRE) at Google with a focus on Google Kubernetes Engine and AI infrastructure (GPUs, TPUs, and storage).  Drew has published guides on using Kubernetes to fine tune LLM models and helped users kickstart their own AI workloads on Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Dylan Page
speakers.title: SRE @ SFCompute | Co-Chair @ K8s SIG Infra | Co-Chair @ CNCF TAG Infrastructure | Maintainer @ Atlantis
speakers.bio: Dylan Page is the SRE at SFCompute, K8s SIG Infra Co-Chair, CNCF TAG Infrastructure Co-Chair, and a maintainer of Atlantis, a CNCF sandbox project. He is currently focused on scaling bare-metal Kubernetes for AI/ML workloads across cloud and on-premises environments. Before Lambda, Dylan spent four years at Autodesk, supporting an internal developer platform, and five years at DigitalOcean, contributing to their global cloud platform.

speakers.name: Eddie Zaneski
speakers.title: Open Source @ Defense Unicorns
speakers.bio: Eddie lives in Denver, CO with his wife and dog. He loves open source and works on the Kubernetes project. When not hacking on random things you'll most likely find him climbing rocks somewhere.

speakers.name: Edmo Vamerlatti Costa
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at Elastic
speakers.bio: Edmo is an experienced software engineer with a passion for emerging technologies. He currently works at Elastic, where he helps develop robust data processing solutions. As an OpenTelemetry Collector contributor, he helps maintain the OpenTelemetry Transformation Language (OTTL), where he is an active contributor and enthusiast.

speakers.name: Eduardo Arango Gutierrez
speakers.title: Senior Systems Software Engineer @NVIDIA
speakers.bio: Eduardo is a Senior Systems Software Engineer at NVIDIA, working on the Cloud Native Technologies team. Eduardo has focused on enabling users to build and deploy containers on distributed environments.

speakers.name: Eduardo Munari
speakers.title: Staff Technical Product Manager
speakers.bio:
Eduardo Munari, skateboarder and drummer in his (limited) free time, works as a Specialist Platform Product Manager and is a Golden Kubestronaut. 

Passionate about leading innovative initiatives and driving technical excellence, he's always exploring emerging technologies and tools that can contribute to the evolution of products, people, and the community.

speakers.name: Eduardo Silva
speakers.title: Fluent Bit :)
speakers.bio: Eduardo is an entrepreneur and Software Engineer. He is one of Fluentd project maintainers and creator of Fluent Bit, a lightweight Logs, Metrics, and Traces processor.

speakers.name: Eitan Yarmush
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineer at Solo.io
speakers.bio: Devoted network engineer and doggy dad. I spend my time hiking, painting, problem solving, and taking care of my new pup. Trying to make the infra space just a little better :)

speakers.name: Ekin Karabulut
speakers.title: AI/ML Developer Advocate
speakers.bio: Ekin is a Developer Advocate at NVIDIA, following the acquisition of Run:ai. Prior to that, she specialized in the privacy implications of federated learning systems with DNNs. Currently, she is exploring the efficient usage of large models in production and one of the maintainers of KAI scheduler, which is a CNCF sandbox project.

speakers.name: Emily Chen
speakers.title: CNCF Ambassador | Solutions Engineer @ Akuity
speakers.bio:
Emily is a solutions engineer at Akuity, an Argo enthusiast, and a CNCF Ambassador. She is an active contributor to various CNCF projects, including translation efforts for ebpf.io and the CNCF Glossary, and an advocate for diversity and inclusion. 

Outside of CNCF, Emily is a contributor to the scikit-learn Machine Learning & Data Science library, a life-long language learner, and a bookworm.

speakers.name: Ender Demirkaya
speakers.title: Senior Engineering Manager
speakers.bio: Ender Demirkaya is a Senior Engineering Manager at Uber. He has worked on building high-performance, distributed systems at Uber, Meta, Microsoft and startups. His focus areas were distributed Key-Value stores (Azure's objectstore), Search Engines (indexing, retrieval, NLP, query processing, ranking, product, privacy, ...) and workflow orchestration engines. He's currently leading the Cadence project under CNCF.

speakers.name: Engin Diri
speakers.title: Pulumi
speakers.bio:
I'm a Senior Solutions Architect at Pulumi in Heilbronn, Germany. Over 15 years I've gone from Java backend to frontend to CI/CD, and now work in DevOps and platform engineering. Mostly Kubernetes and infrastructure as code, with a growing amount of AI. 

Right now I'm poking at AI on Kubernetes, partly to make sense of it and partly to find new ways to make myself redundant.

speakers.name: Eric Ernst
speakers.title: Engineer, Apple Inc.
speakers.bio: Software Engineer at Apple Inc.

speakers.name: Eric Gregory
speakers.title: Senior Technical Writer at Cosmonic
speakers.bio: Eric Gregory is a Senior Technical Writer at Cosmonic, wasmCloud contributor, and Recognized Contributor focusing on documentation in the Bytecode Alliance. A former computer science educator, he lives in Carrboro, North Carolina with his wife and son.

speakers.name: Erica Hughberg
speakers.title: Community Advocate  at Tetrate
speakers.bio:
Erica Hughberg is a technical leader, experienced public speaker, and community advocate passionate about helping engineering teams build scalable, secure, and human-centric platforms for the AI era.

As a maintainer of Envoy AI Gateway, she plays a key role in enabling organizations to securely and efficiently integrate AI-powered services into their systems and solutions.

speakers.name: Erin Walter
speakers.title: Sony Interactive Entertainment (PlayStation), Sr. Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Erin Walter is a Senior Software Engineer at PlayStation, where she builds platform solutions a focus on improved Developer Experience and Productivity Tooling. Her team empowers engineers for excellence, making golden paths accessible, secure, and streamlined.

speakers.name: Evaline Ju
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at IBM Research
speakers.bio: Evaline is a senior engineer working on the AI platform engineering team of IBM Research and based in Denver, Colorado. Her work focuses on platform-level concerns for agent workloads including guardrails and observability. She is also a contributor to the Kubernetes agentic networking group.

speakers.name: Evan Bradley
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at Dynatrace
speakers.bio: Evan helps maintain the OpenTelemetry Collector, where he is a primary contributor to the OpenTelemetry Transformation Language (OTTL), and helps drive adoption of the OpenTelemetry Agent Management Protocol (OpAMP) to enable users to manage fleets of Collectors. Evan has a background in developing DevOps tooling and observability solutions, and is currently a senior software engineer at Dynatrace where he works on data ingestion for open standards with a focus on OpenTelemetry.

speakers.name: Evan Sheng
speakers.title: Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic
speakers.bio: Evan Sheng is a Member of Technical Staff on Anthropic’s Core Infrastructure team, where he builds and scales the infrastructure to power the development of Frontier AI that is beneficial to all. Prior to Anthropic, Evan worked on Kubernetes Autoscaling and Scheduling at both Databricks and Airbnb.

speakers.name: Evelyn (Chungyu) Chen
speakers.title: Sustaining Excellence: From Visibility to Savings, the Evolution of Production Engineering
speakers.bio:
Evelyn (Chungyu) Chen brings 10+ years of production engineering experience at Yahoo, with a track record of driving resilience for iconic platforms including Yahoo Frontpage, Finance, Sports, and pioneering social platforms.

Currently, Evelyn manages Kubernetes and Service Mesh initiatives across multi-cloud and on-premises environments (AWS, GCP, Bare-Metal), focusing on cost optimization, stability, and observability at scale.

speakers.name: Fabian Kammel
speakers.title: Senior Security Consultant, ControlPlane
speakers.bio: Fabian Kammel is a Senior Security Consultant at ControlPlane, where he helps to make the (cloud-native) world a safer place. His goal is to bring hardware security and cloud-native security closer together, as well as, improving the developer experience in the security space. He previously spoke at KubeCon, SigstoreCon, was a guest on the Kubernetes Podcast, and regular host of the CNCF TAG Security.

speakers.name: Fabiano Amaral
speakers.title: Senior Manager - Stone
speakers.bio: Fabiano is a Platform Engineering manager at Stone, leading teams responsible for building Karavela, an internal developer platform. With a strong background in cloud infrastructure, distributed systems, and software engineering, he focuses on scalability, developer experience, and operational excellence across AWS and Azure environments.

speakers.name: Fabrizio Sgura
speakers.title: Chief Engineer (Platform Product Business, Distributed Architecture) at Veritas Automata|CNCF Ambassador|Golden Kubestronaut
speakers.bio: I began my programming journey at the tender age of 12, diving headfirst into Basic and Assembler for Sinclair and Commodore machines back in the distant 1980s, cementing my foundation. I've dived headfirst into the world of information technology, enjoying the constant evolution of systems and technologies, programming languages, being an insatiable learner and a high-level engineer. Scalability and flexibility are my passions. My job is my favorite game.

speakers.name: Faseela Kundattil
speakers.title: Experienced Cloud Native Developer, Ericsson
speakers.bio: Faseela is a cloud-native developer at Ericsson, and a member of the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee. She has given talks and workshops at several conferences evangelizing CNCF projects, including the recent KubeCons. She is a CNCF Ambassador, LFX Mentor, and the winner of the prestigious CNCF “Chop Wood Carry Water” award, 2023. She is also the creator of "Izzy saves the Birthday", a children's illustrated book from Istio.

speakers.name: Fatih E. Nar
speakers.title: Distinguished Chief Architect at Red Hat
speakers.bio: Fatih E. Nar is a Red Hat CTO Office Chief Architect focused on cloud-native, telecom, and AI. Prior roles at Google, Verizon Wireless, Canonical, and Ericsson. In 2025 he was elected AI/ML subject matter expert in Linux Foundation Networking (LFN), steering its AI work. He writes the Open xG HyperCore series on Medium and contributes to AI/ML projects on GitHub and Hugging Face. Off hours: kubectl, new datasets, and the occasional dad joke.

speakers.name: Felicitas Pojtinger
speakers.title: Software Engineer at LiveKit
speakers.bio: Felicitas Pojtinger is a software engineer working on all things cloud native. She has developed multiple popular OSS projects such as the WebRTC-based overlay networking tool weron, the Go network boot server bofied, the go-nbd library and more. Currently, she does research and development in the virtualization space at LiveKit.

speakers.name: Felipe Araujo
speakers.title: Technical Lead at Nubank's Observability team
speakers.bio: Lead software engineer with experience building highly scalable applications in complex scopes, having worked on diverse projects across fintechs and other industries, with a wide range of technologies. Felipe is currently a Technical Lead on Nubank's observability team, building solutions that meet the institution's performance and scalability needs at scale.

speakers.name: Felipe Garcia
speakers.title: NVIDIA, Solutions Architect
speakers.bio: Felipe Garcia is a solutions architect on NVIDIA CSP GTM team, where he helps cloud service providers scale GPU-accelerated AI infrastructure, agents, and models. Before NVIDIA, he worked at AWS, Google, Microsoft and Oracle building and shipping Cloud and AI native solutions.

speakers.name: Filip Křepinský
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineer, Red Hat
speakers.bio: Filip is a software engineer at Red Hat, working on the OpenShift project.

speakers.name: Flynn -
speakers.title: Technical Evangelist, Buoyant
speakers.bio: Flynn is a technical evangelist at Buoyant, educating developers about Linkerd, Kubernetes, and cloud-native development in general. He has spent 40+ years in software, with a common thread of communications and security throughout, and is a coauthor of Linkerd: Up and Running from O'Reilly, a co-lead of the AI Gateway Working Group and Gateway API for service mesh, and the original author of the Emissary-ingress API gateway. He is most easily found as @flynn on the CNCF or Linkerd Slacks.

speakers.name: Francisco Herrera Lira
speakers.title: Red Hat, OSSM QE
speakers.bio: With 15+ years of experience, I embarked on my cloud journey 8 years ago, transitioning from a QE role at NEC Iberica to a DevOps Engineer. Recently, I joined Red Hat as a QE for OpenShift Service Mesh, where my Istio journey continues. I gained hands-on Istio experience at NEC Iberica and deepened my understanding as a Red Hat QE, contributing valuably to the product.

speakers.name: Frank Li
speakers.title: Head of Global Developer Relations
speakers.bio: Frank Li is Head of Global Developer Relations at StepFun, where he works with inference platforms, AI agent builders, developer tools, and open-source projects to bring StepFun models into real-world use. He has experience across multiple startups, and contributed to open-source data infrastructure.

speakers.name: Friedrich Gonzalez
speakers.title: Apple, Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Friedrich is a software engineer with 20 years of experience, currently working at Apple. He is also a an OSS maintainer for Cortex. On his free time, Friedrich likes to play with the cutest doberman puppy there is.

speakers.name: Gaurav Nanda
speakers.title: Databricks | Engineering Manager, Platform Infrastructure
speakers.bio: Gaurav Nanda is an Engineering Manager at Databricks, where he leads platform infrastructure initiatives across networking, traffic management, and reliability for large-scale distributed systems. Previously, he led platform engineering at Harness and was a Tech Lead at Google, working on hyperscale systems.

speakers.name: Gavrish Prabhu
speakers.title: Technical Lead at Nutanix
speakers.bio: Gavrish Prabhu is a Founding ML Engineer on the Nutanix Enterprise AI team with a background in distributed systems and AI Infrastructure. He is active in open-source projects and is a maintainer of KServe and Envoy AI Gateway Projects. His key interests are systems involving the next generation of AI workloads, mainly inference at scale of AI Factories

speakers.name: George Jenkins
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Bloomberg
speakers.bio: George is a software engineer working on Cloud based data analytics and compute platforms for at Bloomberg. He enjoys working with and contributing back to open source, and utilizing the best in technology to solve business problems.

speakers.name: Gorkem Ercan
speakers.title: CTO
speakers.bio: Gorkem Ercan is the CTO and co-founder of Jozu, building open-source infrastructure to bring security and reproducibility to the AI/ML lifecycle. A longtime contributor to cloud-native developer tools, he previously led developer experience at Red Hat. Gorkem bridges platform engineering with MLOps and Generative AI—and continues to shape conversations at the intersection of cloud-native and AI, often before the standards catch up.

speakers.name: Graham Helton
speakers.title: (Too much for Zblock)
speakers.bio: Graham is a Senior Red Team Engineer at Snowflake specializing in Linux and Kubernetes exploitation.

speakers.name: Grant Spence
speakers.title: Red Hat Engineer
speakers.bio:
Grant is an OpenShift Engineer at Red Hat working on evolving the Gateway API offerings. He's an active community member and contributor of Gateway API and CoreDNS.

Grant's aspiration is to continually expand his knowledge and expertise by exploring and innovating with emerging technologies. He possesses a fascination for cloud-based advancements, with a particular interest in Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Graziano Casto
speakers.title: Developer Advocate @ Akuity | Co-Chair @ CNCF TAG DevEx
speakers.bio:
Graziano is a DevRel Engineer at Akamas, where he spends his days convincing computers to stop being lazy and start being efficient. A former distributed systems developer and product manager, he’s now on a mission to optimize the entire cloud-native universe, one Pod at a time. As a Tech Lead for the CNCF TAG DevEx and a member of the Kubernetes Release Team since v1.34, he balances deep infrastructure roots with a passion for developer happiness.

More on: https://castograziano.com/

speakers.name: Greg Bray
speakers.title: Living life one byte at a time
speakers.bio: Greg is a lifelong Utahn and currently works as a Customer Engineer at Google Cloud specializing in building GKE, Service Mesh, and Serverless deployments. Previously Greg worked as an SRE at Reddit, Walmart Labs, and Stack Overflow.

speakers.name: Greg Leffler
speakers.title: Director, Developer Evangelism at Splunk
speakers.bio:
Greg Leffler heads the Observability Developer Evangelism team at Splunk and is on a mission to spread the good word of Observability to the world. 

Greg's career has taken him from the NOC to SRE, from SRE to management, with side stops in security and editorial functions at companies including eBay and LinkedIn. 

In addition to Observability, Greg's professional interests include hiring, training, SRE culture and operating effective remote teams.

speakers.name: Guangya Liu
speakers.title: JPMorgan Chase
speakers.bio: Guangya Liu is an Executive Director at JPMorgan Chase, focusing on AI observability, GPU optimization, and AI inference systems. He is also a seasoned open-source contributor and llm-d SIG observability lead, currently focused on projects such as llm-d, Kueue, and LlamaStack (OGX).

speakers.name: Guilherme Cassolato
speakers.title: Senior Principal Software Engineer @ Red Hat
speakers.bio: Chair of Kubernetes SIG-Network, lead architect of the Kuadrant CNCF project, and creator of Authorino. Guilherme is a Senior Principal Engineer at Red Hat, with deep involvement in Gateway API and Agentic Networking.

speakers.name: Hadrien Patte
speakers.title: Software engineer, Datadog
speakers.bio: Hadrien Patte is a Software Engineer at Datadog and a Cilium committer. He leads the Kubernetes networking team responsible for running and operating Cilium across the company's large multi-cloud Kubernetes infrastructure. His work focuses on the operational side of Cilium at scale: keeping the datapath fast, safe to upgrade, and transparent to the workloads on top.

speakers.name: Han Shen
speakers.title: Dynamia.ai,Frontend Engineer
speakers.bio:
Shen Han is a Frontend Engineer at Dynamia.ai and an active contributor to the HAMi open-source project. She builds user interfaces for GPU resource management and observability in Kubernetes-based AI environments.
Her work focuses on designing visualization systems to help platform engineers understand GPU allocation, workload placement, and cluster resource behavior. Through contributions to HAMi WebUI, she explores how interface design improves the operability of complex AI infrastructure.

speakers.name: Hanhong Gao
speakers.title: VP of Engineering, Verkada
speakers.bio: VP of Engineering at Verkada

speakers.name: Hannah Foxwell
speakers.title: Co-Founder, BIMP
speakers.bio:
With over a decade of experience in technology transformation Hannah has always advocated for the human impact of change. Hannah is relentlessly curious about the tools, technologies, processes and practices that make life better for the people involved in software development, using this knowledge to build happy, high-performing engineering teams.

Hannah is co-founder of BIMP - The Base Image Management Platform and the leader of thriving AI community "AI for the rest of us."

speakers.name: Hannah Olukoye
speakers.title: Google Developer Expert |Engineering Manager
speakers.bio:
Hannah is an Engineering Manager who translates complex software engineering concepts into people-centric strategies. Leveraging her background as a software engineer and Google Developer Expert for Android, she now focuses on building platforms that reduce developer cognitive load and empower teams to move faster and safely. 
She remains an active mentor, technical writer, and international speaker dedicated to motivating others, especially women, to pursue careers in tech.

speakers.name: Hao Jiang
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Hark | Ray & KubeRay Contributor
speakers.bio: Hao Jiang is a Software Engineer at Hark and an open-source contributor to Ray and KubeRay. He focuses on building scalable infrastructure for multi-modal model training on Kubernetes. Previously, he worked on large-scale distributed storage and database systems at xAI, Mooncake Labs, and Nuro. He is also a PMC member of Apache OpenDAL and a leading contributor to the DuckDB ecosystem.

speakers.name: Hardeep Singh Tiwana
speakers.title: Golden Kubestronaut | Senior TAM, AWS | Creator, The Kubernetes Show
speakers.bio: Hardeep Singh Tiwana has spent 25 years breaking and rebuilding infrastructure, from bare-metal Linux in 2000 to production Kubernetes clusters running GPU inference today. Golden Kubestronaut (one of 2 at AWS, 408 worldwide). Major contributor to the EKS Finhack Workshop and Karpenter Workshop. Creator of The Kubernetes Show on YouTube. Built multi-master HA patterns for Kubernetes before kubeadm made it easy. Focuses on failure modes that only surface under pressure.

speakers.name: Hari Krishna Sunder
speakers.title: Architect at YugabyteDB
speakers.bio: Hari Krishna Sunder is an Architect at YugabyteDB, specializing in cloud-native, agentic data systems and distributed architectures. Across 14+ years, he has been a founding member of Azure SQL Database and Azure Synapse Data Warehouse and built core components of YugabyteDB and Meko, a memory layer for multi-agent systems. He serves on the DocumentDB Technical Steering Committee (Linux Foundation) and has spoken at Microsoft Build, Carnegie Mellon, PGConf, DSS, and executive forums.

speakers.name: Harkirat Singh
speakers.title: Software Engineer passionate about Open Source, building things, and helping others.
speakers.bio: At the end of 2022, I began my career as a software engineer by working on CNCF projects. Being selected as an LFX mentee for Fall 2022 was a turning point that accelerated my growth and I also won several hackathons . Recently collaborated with European founders to build solutions, engage with customers, and more.

speakers.name: Harshit Gupta
speakers.title: Microsoft - SDE
speakers.bio: I am a software engineer at Microsoft focusing on virtualization and container runtimes on Kubernetes based platforms.

speakers.name: Heba Elayoty
speakers.title: Microsoft, software enginner
speakers.bio: Heba is a software engineer who is part of Azure Upstream team, previously AKS team. She is an active member of the k8s community for various SIGs and WGs and was part of the 1.18,1.24,1.27, and 1.28 release teams a Bug Triage lead for the 1.25. Worked as a Java developer for 10+ years and as System/Infra Engineer for 8+ years. Heba graduated from Computer Engineering Cairo University, Egypt and lives with her two adorable daughters in California. She loves music, cooking, and community work.

speakers.name: Héléne Durand
speakers.title: HAProxy, Senior Software Developer
speakers.bio: I am a Senior Go Software Developer at HAProxy with over 30 years of experience in software development, spanning from C/C++ to Go. I have a strong passion for creating efficient and scalable solutions. For the past seven years, I have been an avid Kubernetes enthusiast, adept at deploying, managing, and orchestrating containerized applications. I enjoy working alongside my talented colleagues at HAProxy, united by a shared commitment to excellence and innovation.

speakers.name: Hemant Kumar
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Red Hat
speakers.bio: Hemant is a Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat working on storage subsystem of Kubernetes. He is a member of SIG-Storage and author of persistent volume expansion, volume limits, mount options and various instrumentation bits in storage subsystems of Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Henrik Rexed
speakers.title: Dynatrace Cloud Native Advocate
speakers.bio: Henrik is a Cloud Native Advocate at Dynatrace, the leading Observability platform. Prior to Dynatrace, Henrik has worked more than 15 years, as Performance Engineer. Henrik Rexed Is Also one of the Organizer of the conferences named WOPR, KCD Austria and the owner of the Youtube Channel IsitObservable.

speakers.name: Herik Webb
speakers.title: Director of Software Engineering, Capital One
speakers.bio: Herik Webb is a Director of Software Engineering at Capital One, where he leads the enterprise AI/ML training platforms, serving 10,000+ internal users and powering business critical models at the company. A 10-year Capital One veteran and former AWS engineering manager, he's passionate about building high-performing teams through open source engagement and scaling ML infra from classic models to LLMs. Outside of work, he's an avid reader, foodie, and loves to travel.

speakers.name: Hidetsugu Sugiyama
speakers.title: Red Hat
speakers.bio:
Hidetsugu Sugiyama has been with Red Hat for 13 years, is the Chief Architect driving IOWN and AI-RAN projects at the Telco CTO Office. He is a maintainer of CoHDI sandbox.
With over 35 years of experience in the Telco industry, he has worked on distributed systems, programmable networks, SDN/NFV, virtualization, and disaggregated computing.
Currently, he serves as a Board Director alternate at the IOWN Global Forum and a member of the Technical Steering Committee at the AI-RAN Alliance.

speakers.name: Holly Mooneyham
speakers.title: Lead SRE - Cisco Meraki
speakers.bio: Holly has worked in SRE for 9  years, looking after everything from kernel bugs to globe spanning distributed systems. She loves taking things apart to understand how they work and they joy of solving a complicated mystery someone dropped by her desk with. She loves the idea of curiosity as a skill, and one of her favorite things is teaching others to "let's go see". Outside of work you'll find her traveling the world, leading raid groups in Final Fantasy XIV, or making lots of Japanese food.

speakers.name: Hong Sng
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Databricks
speakers.bio: Software Engineer @ Databricks building infrastructure for multi-cloud, multi-model Data and AI workloads at scale.

speakers.name: Hongbing Zhang
speakers.title: Chief Operating Officer Of DaoCloud  KubeEdge TSC Member
speakers.bio: Hongbing Zhang is Chief Operating Officer of DaoCloud. He is a veteran in open source areas, he founded IBM China Linux team in 2011 and organized team to make significant contributions in Linux Kernel/openstack/hadoop projects. Now he is focusing on cloud native domain and leading DaoCloud's edge computing tech/product/business team to continue open source contributions.

speakers.name: Hongcai Ren
speakers.title: Huawei, Senior Software Engineer, Karmada
speakers.bio:
Hongcai Ren(@RainbowMango) is the CNCF Ambassador, who has been working on Kubernetes and other CNCF projects since 2019,
and is the maintainer of the Kubernetes and Karmada projects.

speakers.name: Hoon Jo
speakers.title: CNCF Ambassador, AI & Cloud-Native Engineer
speakers.bio: Hoon Jo is a CNCF Ambassador and Kubestronaut who has spoken at KubeCon North America, Europe, China, and India across multiple years. He is the author of multiple books on Kubernetes and AI-assisted operations, and serves as a program committee reviewer for CNCF regional conferences.

speakers.name: Hope Hadfield
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Red Hat
speakers.bio: Hope Hadfield is a Software Engineer at Red Hat in Toronto, passionate about contributing to Open Source projects and enabling others to do the same. She had her start in the Open Source community working as a maintainer of the VS Code Java plugin and a diligent committer for the Eclipse Foundation. These days, she works on Red Hat Developer Hub and its upstream project Backstage, where she is a maintainer of Backstage Community Plugins.

speakers.name: Hrittik Roy
speakers.title: Software Engineer | CNCF Ambassador
speakers.bio: Hrittik is a Platform Advocate at vCluster Labs and a CNCF Ambassador with expertise in cloud native technologies and open source communities. He has contributed extensively to developer advocacy, technical writing, and community engagement. Hrittik has keynoted events such as the MCP Dev Summits and delivered talks at KubeCons, KCDs, Open Source Summits, and more. He has also served as a Program Committee member for several CloudNativeCons.

speakers.name: Huan Wei
speakers.title: Kubernetes, edge computing, high performance computing, etc
speakers.bio: CNCF Amabassador, CNCF KubeEdge Maintainer & TSC member, KubeCon Europe 2023,  2025, 2026 speaker, KubeCon 2025 NA speaker, KubeCon 2025 HongKong speaker, KubeCon Shanghai 2026 Speaker

speakers.name: Hussaina Begum Nandyala
speakers.title: Senior Staff Engineer, Netskope
speakers.bio: Hussaina Begum is a technology leader and innovator, with focus on Systems and Network security. She had designed and implemented security solutions and protocols for IBM, Citrix, Cisco, VMware and Netskope. Hussaina is one of the maintainers at Meshery project since 2021.

speakers.name: Ian Rudie
speakers.title: Istio at Solo.io
speakers.bio: From a background in Unix and deep infrastructure Ian joined T-Mobile in a position leading development on a distributed Kubernetes operator to manage a cloud-native API gateway as well as managing Istio on 100+ clusters. Presently thrilled to be on the Open Source team at Solo.io as a software engineer focusing on Istio.

speakers.name: Idit Levine
speakers.bio: Idit Levine is the founder and CEO of Solo.io, where she is dedicated to simplifying agentic AI and empowering organizations to embrace cloud-native technologies. With a strong background in distributed systems and cloud infrastructure, Idit is passionate about transforming complex challenges into accessible, practical solutions for teams of all sizes by leveraging the power of innovative open-source technologies.

speakers.name: Imma Valls
speakers.title: Grafana Labs, Staff Developer Advocate
speakers.bio: Imma is a Staff Developer Advocate at Grafana Labs with over 25 years in tech, passionate about simplifying Observability, OpenTelemetry, and Cloud-Native architectures. She focuses on creating deep technical content and driving best practices within the community. She is also a passionate community builder and ally who advocates for underrepresented groups. You will find her organizing Grafana, AI Socratic, Cloud Native, DevOpsDays, and TechFems community events in Barcelona.

speakers.name: Ingy döt Net
speakers.title: Invented YAML
speakers.bio: Ingy döt Net is one of the original inventors of the YAML data language, and its primary maintainer. He is also the maintainer of go-yaml, Go's primary YAML library, used by kubernetes and its ecosystem.

speakers.name: Isaac Wilson
speakers.title: The Trade Desk, Staff Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Isaac is a Staff Software Engineer at The Trade Desk specializing in distributed systems and networking. He led a global scale migration for The Trade Desk’s Load Balancing infrastructure from bare-metal HAProxy to Kubernetes Gateway API and while doing so contributed multiple features to EnvoyGateway such as Zone Aware Routing as well as other enhancements upstream to Envoy.

speakers.name: Isala Piyarisi
speakers.title: Maintainer of OpenChoreo
speakers.bio: Isala Piyarisi is an Associate Tech Lead Engineer at WSO2 and a core maintainer of OpenChoreo, a CNCF Sandbox developer platform, where he works on networking. He holds the CKA and CKS certifications and has spent over 7 years in cloud native.

speakers.name: Itamar Holder
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineer, Red Hat
speakers.bio:
Kubevirt maintainer, Kubernetes sig-node developer.
Leading the development of swap support in Kubernetes.

I have a deep love for open-source software and a passion for complex, large-scale systems with many moving parts. I absolutely thrive on giving talks at conferences, where I can discuss and share ideas with the community.

speakers.name: Ivan Valdes Castillo
speakers.title: Independent
speakers.bio: Ivan is a Site Reliability Engineer specializing in CI/CD pipelines, Infrastructure as Code, and automation. His dedication to spreading and mentoring the DevOps culture is evident in his efforts to foster collaboration and streamline development. In his free time, he is an active Kubernetes and etcd contributor, balancing his Karma. When he's not in front of a keyboard, you can find him running in the mountains, homebrewing beer, or building Lego cars with his son.

speakers.name: Jaana Dogan
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Google
speakers.bio: Jaana is one of the tech leads leading Google's ML/AI systems, specifically focusing on agentic serving and distributed runtimes, including new storage and compute infrastructure.

speakers.name: Jack Francis
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineer, Microsoft
speakers.bio:
Jack works on open source Kubernetes from his basement in Portland, Oregon, USA.

When he’s not working, he’s usually upstairs hanging out with his family. On occasion he straps on a guitar and turns the amp to 11.

speakers.name: Jack Ma
speakers.title: Microsoft, Principal Engineer
speakers.bio: I have 20+ years of full-stack software engineering/managing experience, excelling in both individual contribution and leadership capacity. I architect/code/operate cloud systems, big and small, for years and made popular pixel-perfect pages. I lead by example and make both the team and the project awesome. I am a lifelong learner and have always been ready for new challenges.

speakers.name: Jackie Maertens
speakers.title: Microsoft, Senior Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Software engineer at Microsoft. Member of the Azure Container Upstream team and Istio security maintainer. Co-lead of Istio's product security working group.

speakers.name: Jacob Aronoff
speakers.title: Founding Engineer at Tero
speakers.bio: Jacob Aronoff is a founding engineer at Tero and an OpenTelemetry maintainer for the OpenTelemetry Operator project. He's spent his career in a variety of backend roles acting as a distributed systems engineer, an SRE and a DevOps professional. Jacob's focus is enabling customers to reliably send telemetry data with a focus on Kubernetes and OpenTelemetry.

speakers.name: Jacquie Capur
speakers.title: Sr. Developer Advocate at Nebius
speakers.bio: Jacquie Capur is a Senior Developer Advocate at Nebius, where she builds with AI—from cloud infrastructure to physical AI and robots. Since 2015, she’s worked across multicloud platforms, Infrastructure as Code, and compliance-grade environments. A frequent speaker at AWS re:Invent, HashiConf, DevOpsDays, and Grace Hopper Celebration, she shares practical lessons from experimenting, building, and shipping under pressure.

speakers.name: Jago Macleod
speakers.title: Engineering Director, Kubernetes & GKE, Google
speakers.bio: Jago Macleod is an Engineering Director at Google, where he leads much of the Kubernetes and Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) team, which gives him the opportunity to work with some of Google Cloud’s largest customers. Prior to working at Google, Jago helped make the smart homes that may eventually turn against us at Nest; and before that, he made some of the games that will distract us along the way as VP of Engineering at Disney Interactive Games.

speakers.name: Jake Hulberg
speakers.title: Founding Developer Advocate, Infisical
speakers.bio: Jake Hulberg is the Founding Developer Advocate at Infisical, the open source security platform for secrets, certificates, privileged access, and AI agent access. He creates demos, videos, and guides that teach developers how to manage secrets securely, run PKI, and control privileged access, for both people and AI agents. He also runs Jake's Tech (@jakestechjourney) on YouTube.

speakers.name: Jake Pineda
speakers.title: Open Source Growth Strategist, Senior Membership Executive, CNCF
speakers.bio: Open source, cloud-native, and AI strategist driving ecosystem growth for the Linux Foundation and CNCF. I design engagement models that bring the world's largest companies into community governance and turn complex technical needs into sustainable revenue. Actively shaping the intersection of AI and cloud-native infrastructure through conformance, policy, and adoption frameworks. Financially rigorous, equity-minded, and backing the movement across Latin America and underserved communities.

speakers.name: Jakub Scholz
speakers.title: Engineer @ Cloudera
speakers.bio: Jakub is a CNCF Ambassador and engineer at Cloudera with deep expertise in Kubernetes, streaming, and messaging. As a co-founder and maintainer of the Strimzi project, he has spent years bridging the gap between Apache Kafka and cloud-native infrastructure. Before his time at Cloudera, Jakub worked at Red Hat and in the financial sector, bringing a wealth of real-world operational experience to the open-source community.

speakers.name: Jakub Suchy
speakers.title: Solutions Engineer
speakers.bio: Jakub Suchy is the Director of Solutions Engineering at HAProxy Technologies, where he designs and prototypes solutions for application delivery and load balancing infrastructure. With his background in Linux infrastructure and Open Source Applications, he specializes in developing innovative approaches to modern application delivery challenges, focusing on micro-services architecture and high-availability systems

speakers.name: James Spurin
speakers.title: CNCF Ambassador, Docker Captain, Founder and CEO of DiveInto
speakers.bio:
James Spurin, a CNCF Ambassador, Docker Captain and a Technical Course Creator has educated over 100K students in Cloud Native, DevOps and Kubernetes.

His 25-year career includes management, engineering and software development at Nomura, Goldman Sachs, Dell EMC, and Demon Internet.

As a trusted figure in Cloud Native, James combines his extensive experience with his passion for teaching to promote understanding and adoption of cloud native technologies.

speakers.name: Jamie Danielson
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at Honeycomb.io
speakers.bio: Jamie is a Senior Software Engineer at Honeycomb where she works on instrumentation libraries and agent observability. She is an active contributor to multiple OpenTelemetry projects, and a maintainer for OpenTelemetry JavaScript.

speakers.name: Jan Bronicki
speakers.title: Microsoft, Flatcar, Open-source
speakers.bio: Jan Bronicki is a software engineer at Microsoft and a maintainer of Flatcar Container Linux, a CNCF project that provides a minimal, secure, and immutable operating system for running containers at scale. He is passionate about open source, cloud native infrastructure, and building reliable systems through collaboration. His work spans operating system maintenance, automation, security, and community-driven development.

speakers.name: Jan Wozniak
speakers.title: KEDA maintainer
speakers.bio: Jan is a software engineer who spends most of his time with open-source technologies. He contributed to and helped to maintain various parts of the Kubernetes ecosystem.

speakers.name: Janet Kuo
speakers.title: Google
speakers.bio: Janet Kuo is a Senior Staff Software Engineer at Google Cloud and a member of the Kubernetes Steering Committee. She has been shaping Kubernetes since before its 1.0 launch in 2015. She is the co-chair and Tech Lead of SIG Apps, leads Kubernetes AI Conformance, and is a KubeCon co-chair emeritus. When not immersed in Kubernetes, she enjoys exploring the world through travel and photography.

speakers.name: Jared Watts
speakers.title: Founding Engineer - Upbound
speakers.bio: Jared Watts is a Founding Engineer at Upbound, where he is working on advancing cloud-native computing by enabling anyone to build their own cloud platform. He is also a co-creator of the open source Crossplane (https://crossplane.io) and Rook (https://rook.io) projects. Prior to Upbound, Jared worked on P2P storage distributed across the public internet at Symform, a startup later acquired by Quantum. Jared began his career at Microsoft working on applications for Windows Server management.

speakers.name: Jason Deal
speakers.title: Software Engineer, AWS
speakers.bio: I'm a software engineer at AWS, working on EKS Auto Mode and Karpenter

speakers.name: Jason Plumb
speakers.title: OpenTelemetry maintainer / Splunk senior principal engineer
speakers.bio: Jason Plumb (he/him) is a hacker, artist, experimenter, polyglot programmer, and dad from Portland, OR, USA. He is co-maintainer of OpenTelemetry Android and an approver in various OpenTelemetry java projects. When not at work, Jason volunteers with Futel to install and maintain a network of free public payphones. He also builds synthesizers, experiments with sound, screens classic cult films, and rides steel-frame bicycles.

speakers.name: Jason Schechner
speakers.title: Traversal's First SRE Researcher and AI Adoption Engineer
speakers.bio: SRE with a career older than the term "SRE".  I've done it all, seen it all, and (hopefully) learned at least a few lessons along the way.  Life-long tinkerer, habitual puzzle-solver, SCUBA diver and enthusiast for anything interesting.

speakers.name: Jason Stryker
speakers.title: Kubernetes Community of Practice Lead @ Capital One
speakers.bio: Jason is a engineering leader with extensive experience implementing Kubernetes and Cloud Native technology in highly regulated environments. As the Community of Practice lead for Kubernetes at Capital One, he exudes a deep passion for open source and community governance models exemplified by CNCF hosted projects.

speakers.name: Jay Jackson
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer - CallRevu
speakers.bio: Jay Jackson is a Senior Software Engineer at CallRevu, based in Houston, Texas. He brings over 2 decades of experience in the tech industry, primarily as QA and Software Engineer. Jay has navigated this tech journey as a deaf individual, with American Sign Language (ASL) as his primary mode of communication and is passionate about exploring ways to improve accessibility for Deaf and Hard of Hearing community.

speakers.name: Jayanth Varavani
speakers.title: AWS, Software Development Manager at EKS
speakers.bio: Jayanth is a Software Development Manager on the AWS EKS Networking team. He has several years of experience in the networking domain and serves as a maintainer of the EKS CNI and Network Policy project. Jayanth is deeply passionate about eBPF and actively leads multiple eBPF-related initiatives within EKS. You can find him on GiHub as @jayanthvn

speakers.name: Jed Salazar
speakers.title: Security Solutions Architect
speakers.bio: Jed Salazar started his Security and SRE journey working on Borg clusters and securing Alphabet companies at Google. He's passionate about security and SRE and spreading knowledge to benefit everyone in the community. In his free time, he enjoys trail running the mountains of Boulder, Colorado.

speakers.name: Jeff Hoffman
speakers.title: VP of Container Services, OCI
speakers.bio: Jeff Hoffman is a Vice President at Oracle, where he leads the Container, Kubernetes, and Serverless organization for Oracle Cloud Infrastructure (OCI). His team is responsible for OCI services including Oracle Kubernetes Engine (OKE), Container Instances, and Functions. Jeff has over 30 years of experience in cloud and engineering leadership, including work prior to Oracle at Amazon, Samsung, HashiCorp, and Dell.

speakers.name: Jeff Spahr
speakers.title: Director, AI/ML Infrastructure & Platform - Capital One
speakers.bio: Jeff Spahr is a Director in the AI/ML organization at Capital One, focused on scaling high-performing infrastructure and platform teams. A long-time Kubernetes enthusiast, his passion for infrastructure spans global-scale cloud deployments to the Raspberry Pi cluster in his home office. Jeff enjoys sharing lessons learned at conferences like KubeCon, SREcon, and All Things Open. He lives in Raleigh, NC, with his wife and two children.

speakers.name: Jeffrey Sica
speakers.title: Head of Projects @ CNCF
speakers.bio: Jeffrey (@jeefy) is Head of Projects at the CNCF, with a focus on improving community and project automation. Before that, he worked at Red Hat and the University of Michigan focusing on Cloud Native technologies and CI/CD patterns. Jeffrey has been a contributor to upstream Kubernetes, helping in SIG-Contribex, SIG-Release, and SIG-UI. He passionately advocates for open source development and recognizing and alleviating burnout.

speakers.name: Jeffrey Ying
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Google
speakers.bio: Jeffrey is a contributor to Kubernetes, mainly working in the SIG apimachinery and CLI space. He had led and been involved with many features such as Server Side Apply, Aggregated Discovery, and OpenAPI V3.

speakers.name: Jeffry Hernández
speakers.title: Site Reliability Engineer
speakers.bio: Senior SRE @ Wizeline with a strong background in cloud infrastructure and Open Source technologies. Co-organizer of CNCG Cali and KCD Colombia. Last year He has been deeply involved in Al Infrastructure, helping customers to serve models at scale and implement best observability practices.

speakers.name: Jennifer Weir
speakers.title: Ford - Kubernetes Platform Engineer
speakers.bio: Jennifer Weir is a Kubernetes Platform Engineer at Ford Motor Company, where she focuses on cloud infrastructure at scale, cluster automation, resource management, and platform reliability. She holds a B.S. in Computer Science from the University of Michigan–Ann Arbor.

speakers.name: Jenny Vega
speakers.title: Senior ML Platform Software Engineer @ Isomorphic Labs
speakers.bio: Jenny Vega is a Senior ML Platform Engineer at Isomorphic Labs, building the infrastructure for AI-driven drug discovery. Specializing in Kubernetes orchestration, Jenny designed and rolled out scheduling enhancements that boosted GPU cluster utilization across tens of millions of monthly runs. Previously, she was a Senior Solutions Architect at Google and AWS, guiding enterprises and startups on distributed training and large-scale cloud architectures.

speakers.name: Jeroen van Erp
speakers.title: Technology Advocate @ SUSE
speakers.bio:
Jeroen van Erp is a Technology Advocate at SUSE, active open source contributor, and Cloud Native speaker, helping developers and platform engineers build open, portable, and resilient infrastructure.
With a background spanning engineering, architecture, and product management, he distills complex topics like Kubernetes, observability, cloud-native security, and open source, into actionable insights.
When not on stage, he's a Rancher at heart, herding his sheep in the Netherlands.

speakers.name: Jesper Joergensen
speakers.title: Co-founder, CPO, ConfigHub
speakers.bio: Started in 2024 with Brian Grant and Alexis Richardson to rethink how configuration for software infrastructure is managed. Before ConfigHub, Jesper was a product leader at Heroku, API product manager at Salesforce, and later ran Twilio's Voice & Video business. His work has centered on platform-as-a-service and developer tools, and on the gap between the elegant experience developers get when writing code and the far rougher experience of operating it.

speakers.name: Jesse Butler
speakers.title: Principal PMT, Amazon EKS
speakers.bio: Jesse is a product manager for Amazon EKS focused on helping customers do more with Kubernetes. He started his career in software more than two decades ago, working up the stack from driver development into userspace and container runtimes. He's been working with containers for several years, and has contributed to the OCI specifications and the Kubernetes release team.

speakers.name: Jessica Forrester
speakers.title: Senior Distinguished Engineer & Chief Architect AI Catalyst Engineering, Red Hat
speakers.bio: Jessica Forrester is a Senior Distinguished Engineer and the Chief Architect for AI Catalyst Engineering at Red Hat, working at the intersection of AI and cloud native as new technologies move into the Red Hat AI product portfolio. She was an early contributor to Red Hat OpenShift, Kubernetes, and their related communities. She has led many cross-functional engineering teams at Red Hat across AI, hybrid cloud services, and Kubernetes / OpenShift Container Platform.

speakers.name: Jian Cheung
speakers.title: Anthropic, Member of Technical Staff
speakers.bio: Jian is a Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic working on large accelerator clusters. Prior to Anthropic, Jian worked on Compute Infrastructure at Airbnb.

speakers.name: Jian Li
speakers.title: Building AI-Ready Kubernetes Infrastructure for On-Prem and Beyond
speakers.bio: Jian Li is currently working as a principal research engineer at SK Telecom (SKT), and he is also serving as a member of ONOS TST at Open Networking Foundation (ONF). He previously worked as an open source developer at ONF. Jian is currently serving as the chief architect for the Petasus AI Cloud project, which aims to deliver cost-efficient, high-performance AI infrastructure optimized for heterogeneous AI workloads, including both training and inference.

speakers.name: Jim Beyers
speakers.title: VP of Developer Experience - CVS
speakers.bio: Hey there! I'm Jim on the CVS DevEx team, blending my love for tech with making life easier for developers. After stints at Target and Capital One, I've learned to connect tech and business. Originally from Wisconsin, I landed in Minneapolis and collected degrees like Pokémon cards (BA in CS, MS in Software Engineering, MBA from St. Thomas). Off hours, I'm with my wife Nora, kids Amelia and Ben, and our husky Cali Bean. Big on music, concerts, films, and Age of Empires 2.

speakers.name: Jim Bugwadia
speakers.title: Founder and CEO at Nirmata
speakers.bio: Jim Bugwadia is a co-founder and the CEO of Nirmata, the Kubernetes policy and governance company. Jim is an active contributor in the cloud native community and currently serves as co-chair of the Kubernetes Policy and Multi-Tenancy Working Groups. Jim is also a co-creator and maintainer of Kyverno, the policy engine built for Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Jing Chen
speakers.title: Software Engineer at IBM Research
speakers.bio: Jing Chen is a software engineer at IBM Research, where she works on Generative AI infrastructure, benchmarking, and capacity planning for distributed LLM inference on Kubernetes. She is a contributor to open-source projects including llm-d using AI-native simulation methodologies.

speakers.name: Jing Hu
speakers.title: Software Engineer - eBay
speakers.bio: Software Engineer building observability platforms at eBay

speakers.name: JJ Jordan
speakers.title: Member of Technical Staff at Cohere
speakers.bio: JJ Jordan is a Member of Technical Staff on Cohere’s Internal Infrastructure team, where he builds orchestration, scheduling, and reliability systems to improve utilization of large-scale GPU training clusters. He previously spent 17 years at Microsoft working on Visual Studio, Azure observability, and distributed systems built on Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Joe Betz
speakers.title: Technical lead, Kubernetes, SIG api-machinery
speakers.bio: Joe Betz is a tech lead of the Kubernetes api-machinery SIG. Joe has contributed to extensibility features including custom resources, admission webhooks, and CEL. Joe has also contributed to etcd as a project maintainer.

speakers.name: Joe Julian
speakers.title: Sr. Technical Lead, Omniva
speakers.bio:
Joe Julian is a Senior Technical Lead at Omniva, building self-service Kubernetes platforms for AI training and inference on bare-metal GPU clusters. His work spans multi-tenancy, networking, storage, and infrastructure lifecycle management.

A Helm contributor, he uses Flux, GitOps, and custom operators to deploy infrastructure and applications. He uses AI agents for development, testing, documentation, and operations.

Outside work, he enjoys sailing and building useful things.

speakers.name: Joe Kutner
speakers.title: Architect at Salesforce, Co-founder of Buildpacks
speakers.bio: Joe is co-founder of the Cloud Native Buildpacks project, which aims to make containerization more secure and more developer friendly. He started the project in 2018 while working as DX Architect at Salesforce Heroku, and today is the DX Architect for Salesforce’s Hyperforce platform. He’s also the author of The Health Programmer.

speakers.name: Joe Lanford
speakers.title: Red Hat - Senior Principal Software Engineer - Operator Framework
speakers.bio:
Joe is a Senior Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat and leads the OpenShift Operator Framework team. His primary focus is on designing and building OLMv1 and related tooling to make Kubernetes package management as simple, secure, and flexible as OS package management.

In addition to his work in Operator Framework projects, he has been active in the upstream kubebuilder, controller-runtime, and controller-tools projects.

If you have controller or CRD questions, I (hopefully) have answers!

speakers.name: Joe Zhou
speakers.title: Joe Zhou, Lead Developer Advocate @JuiceFS
speakers.bio:
Joe is a cloud-native advocate for storage systems and former startup CTO who excels at leading and motivating team members to deliver exceptional results.

He currently serves as the Lead Developer Advocate in North America at JuiceFS (a high-performance distributed file system) and helps AI/ML engineers, developers, and platform teams get the most out of JuiceFS for performance and efficiency.

speakers.name: Joe Nathan Abellard
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer, Bloomberg | CNCF Karmada Maintainer
speakers.bio:
Joe Nathan Abellard is a Senior Software Engineer on the Cloud Native Compute Services (CNCS) Platform Engineering team at Bloomberg, and a maintainer of the CNCF Karmada project. He's the lead engineer and product owner for Bloomberg's large-scale, managed multi-cluster Kubernetes platform, built on Karmada, enabling the firm's engineering teams to meet the organization's high-availability (HA) mandate across distributed
infrastructure, without requiring deep multi-cluster expertise.

speakers.name: Johan Fylling
speakers.title: OPA Maintainer
speakers.bio: I've been working as a software developer in the IAM space since 2008. In 2021 I joined The OPA team.

speakers.name: John Belamaric
speakers.title: Google, Kubernetes SIG Architecture and WG Device Management Co-chair
speakers.bio:
John is a Sr Staff SWE, co-chair of K8s SIG Architecture and K8s WG Device Management, helping lead efforts to improve how GPUs, TPUs, NICs and other devices are selected, shared, and configured in Kubernetes. He is also co-founder of Nephio, an LF project for K8s-based automation, and a maintainer of CoreDNS, a CNCF project for DNS-based service discovery.

John holds three patents, and is co-author of "Learning CoreDNS" from O’Reilly and "OpenStack Cloud Application Development" from Wiley.

speakers.name: John Howard
speakers.title: Senior Architect at Solo.io
speakers.bio: John Howard is a Senior Architect at Solo.io and Istio Technical Oversight Committee member.

speakers.name: John Kastner
speakers.title: Cedar Dev and Senior Applied Scientist at AWS
speakers.bio: John is an applied scientist at AWS who has been working on the Cedar policy language since its inception three years ago. Prior to that he worked on open-source tooling for semi-automated conversion from C into Checked C, a spatially-memory-safe variant of C, after graduating from the University of Maryland with a masters degree in computer science.

speakers.name: John Kjell
speakers.title: Engineering Manager - Docker
speakers.bio: John is an Engineering Manager at Docker, building an agentic software factory to patch all the things. Previously at ControlPlane, he helped security-conscious organizations build and assure mission-critical platforms. He is a member of the in-toto Steering Committee and maintainer of the Witness and Archivista projects. He also serves as a co-chair of the CNCF's TAG Security. In the OpenSSF, John is a member of the inaugural Ambassador cohort and contributes to the SBOMit project.

speakers.name: Johnu George
speakers.title: Technical Director
speakers.bio: Johnu George is a Technical Director at Nutanix specializing in machine learning systems and cloud-native AI platforms. An active open-source contributor, he has led collaborations across Kubeflow, KServe, and Knative. His interests include ML systems and distributed learning infrastructure. He is a maintainer of KServe and Envoy AI Gateway, and Co-Chair of the Kubeflow Training and AutoML Working Group.

speakers.name: Jon Huhn
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Microsoft
speakers.bio: Jon Huhn is a Software Engineer at Microsoft working on CNCF projects like CAPZ and DRA in Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Jonathan Norris
speakers.title: Director, Software Engineering @ Dynatrace · OpenFeature Governance Board Member · Formerly Co-Founder & CTO, DevCycle
speakers.bio: Jonathan Norris is Director of Software Engineering at Dynatrace, leading feature management engineering after Dynatrace acquired DevCycle, the developer-first feature management platform he co-founded and led as CTO. He serves on the OpenFeature Governance Board, helping advance vendor-neutral feature flagging standards, and focuses on progressive delivery, continuous deployment, release safety, and measuring what matters.

speakers.name: Jooho lee
speakers.title: Red Hat, Principal Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Jooho Lee is a Toronto-based technology professional with over a decade of experience at Red Hat, working across cloud-native platforms and AI. He is on the OpenShift AI Model Serving team, integrating KServe and LLM-D into Open Data Hub to enable production-grade, Kubernetes-native deployment and operation of AI/ML models. He is also a KServe committer, contributing to the project’s model serving and LLM inference.

speakers.name: Jordan Keister
speakers.title: Red Hat Principal Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Jordan is a maintainer for the Operator Framework project and a FOSS contributor for over a decade.  He works with Red Hat helping folks reason about cluster installables and the ecologies required to make them sustainable.

speakers.name: Jordan Liggitt
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Google
speakers.bio: Jordan Liggitt is a software engineer at Google, and helps lead Kubernetes authentication, authorization, and API server efforts.

speakers.name: Jorge Castro
speakers.title: Let's keep the modern world running, sustainably.
speakers.bio:
Jorge O. Castro is a community engineer, specializing in Open Source. He's basically a cat herder – a combination of engineering, developer relations, and user advocacy. 

These days Jorge is the Technical Program Management Director at the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, where he's tasked with helping make open source sustainable. He has worked on Ubuntu, Kubernetes, Kubeflow, Cloud Custodian, and Project Bluefin.

speakers.name: Jorge Palma
speakers.title: Principal PM Lead - AKS
speakers.bio: Jorge is the Principal PM Lead for AKS where he serves thousands of customers and mission critical application and helped lead the service to become the fastest growing service in Azure’s history. Formerly he was the Technical Lead for App Dev and DevOps with the Azure Global Black Belt team and has implemented and architected solutions in Azure since 2012, spanning across different roles from Services, Tech Evangelism and Tech Sales. He holds a MSc in Computer Engineering.

speakers.name: Joseph Sandoval
speakers.title: Adobe Inc, Principal Product Mgr, Developer Platforms
speakers.bio: Joseph Sandoval is a platform engineering and distributed systems practitioner with 25 years across SRE, DevOps, cloud-native infrastructure, and production operations. He focuses on making AI/ML and agentic workloads safe to run on shared platforms through isolation, identity, observability, policy, cost controls, and developer self-service. He is a member of the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee and Vice Chair of the CNCF End User Technical Advisory Board.

speakers.name: Josh Berkus
speakers.title: Kubernetes @ Red Hat
speakers.bio: Josh Berkus is the Kubernetes Community Manager, working in Red Hat's Open Source Program Office.   He's currently involved with Kubernetes, Etcd, Elekto, Podman, and uBlue, but has spent more than 20 years contributing to many projects, including Linux, OpenOffice, PostgreSQL, and Django.  He lives in Portland with a librarian, a pottery studio, and an absurdly large cat.

speakers.name: Juan Bernal
speakers.title: CVS Health, Feature Flagging Engineer
speakers.bio: Juan Bernal is a Staff Engineer at CVS Health, specializing in web development and feature flagging platforms. With a strong background in software engineering practices, he drives library adoption and advocates for web standards. Passionate about innovation, he enjoys exploring new technologies and methodologies. Outside of work, Juan has a soft spot for soft serve ice cream.

speakers.name: Juan David Arguello Plata
speakers.title: Lead of OSPO at Bancolombia
speakers.bio:
Juan David is a leader with experience in cloud-native computing, software development, and IT infrastructure. He serves as the Lead of the Open-Source Program Office at Bancolombia.

Regarding his academic background, Juan David is doing a MSc in CS at the University of Bath, UK, and has a postgraduate degree in AI and ML from The University of Texas at Austin. He is also an active contributor to the tech community who holds the title of Kubestronaut.

speakers.name: Juho Syrjänen
speakers.title: Platform Engineer @ ŌURA
speakers.bio:
🤝 A Platform Engineer
💛  GitOps 

An infrastructure and platform engineer with over 10 years of experience spanning datacenters, DevOps consulting, and platform development. Juho has spent the past several years helping teams tame complex systems and build resilient platforms.

Currently, Juho is working as a Platform Engineer at ŌURA, where he’s building an internal developer platform supporting smart rings worn by millions. .

speakers.name: Jui-An Huang
speakers.title: Anyscale, Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Jui-An Huang is also known as rueian on GitHub. He is the creator of rueidis/valkey-go, an official Redis/Valkey Go client, and more recently has been contributing to Ray and KubeRay since 2022.

speakers.name: Julia Furst Morgado
speakers.title: Principal Developer Relations Engineer
speakers.bio:
Julia helps teams improve system reliability, observability, and scalability by guiding the adoption of modern infrastructure and operational practices.
Beyond her work, Julia is a a Community Manager to the OpenTelemetry project, CNCF Ambassador, AWS Container Hero, Docker Captain, Google Women Techmakers Ambassador, and Girl Code Ambassador. She’s an active community leader who helps organize KCD NY, AWS Community Day NY, and the Cloud Native Meetup NYC.

speakers.name: Juliano Costa
speakers.title: CNCF Ambassador | Principal Developer Relations Engineer at Dash0
speakers.bio: Juliano Costa is a Developer Advocate with a focus on OpenTelemetry. He is a CNCF Ambassador passionate about fostering the Cloud Native community and spreading OTel's word everywhere he goes. Juliano is an active contributor to the OpenTelemetry project and a maintainer on the OpenTelemetry Demo, as well as on the Developer Experience SIG. When he's not talking about OTel, you'll find him chasing after his energetic 3-year-old son.

speakers.name: Juliano Martinez
speakers.title: Principal Engineer at Adyen
speakers.bio: Principal Engineer at Adyen with 25 years of experience in Linux, networking, large-scale infrastructure, and automation. His work spans cloud-native platforms, Kubernetes, service networking, observability, and distributed systems. An open-source enthusiast and Go developer, he approaches systems from first principles and builds simple, composable tools that reduce operational complexity.

speakers.name: Julie Gunderson
speakers.title: Graduate Student
speakers.bio: Julie Gunderson has spent over a decade in tech in leadership and developer advocacy roles at AWS, PagerDuty, Gremlin, and Freeman & Forrest. Her work spans reliability, incident response, DevOps, and community building. She founded and organized DevOpsDays Boise for five years. After years speaking about psychological safety and burnout, she is pursuing a master’s in Clinical Mental Health Counseling, shifting her focus from reliable systems to the well-being of the people who run them.

speakers.name: Julien Semaan
speakers.title: VP R&D @Kubex | CNCF TAG DevEx Tech Lead
speakers.bio: Julien is the VP of Research & Development at Kubex and a Tech Lead with the CNCF TAG for Developer Experience. With deep roots in open source and cloud-native systems, he has been working with Kubernetes since 2017 and has led multiple product transitions to cloud-native architectures.

speakers.name: Juraci Paixão Kröhling
speakers.title: Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Juraci Paixão Kröhling is a software engineer at OllyGarden, a maintainer of the OpenTelemetry project, a member of the project's governing board and CNCF Ambassador. He has presented about distributed tracing, OpenTelemetry, and other related topics at conferences like KubeCon, OpenSource Summit, FOSDEM, and a few DevOpsDays, among others. Previously, he was also a maintainer of both the OpenTracing and Jaeger projects, having also delivered talks about those projects.

speakers.name: Justin Garrison
speakers.title: Field CTO
speakers.bio: Justin is a tinkerer and Field CTO and Sidero Labs. He builds ridiculous contraptions and shares them on the internet to make people smile. He also helps companies solve real world infrastructure problems at large and small scales.

speakers.name: Justin Munoz
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineer, Kinexys by J.P.Morgan
speakers.bio: Justin is a Principal Software Engineer helping teams run Kubernetes workloads with confidence. He’s passionate about making the ‘right way’ the easy way, so teams can spend more time shipping and less time fighting the platform.

speakers.name: Justin O’Leary
speakers.title: Principal Engineer & Security Researcher
speakers.bio: Justin OLeary is a security researcher who focuses on cloud-native infrastructure vulnerabilities. His work on confused deputy flaws in Kubernetes operators has uncovered privilege escalation paths in Config Connector, AWS Controllers for Kubernetes, Azure Service Operator, Crossplane, and other major projects. He is presenting related research at Black Hat USA 2026. By day, he serves as Principal Bioinformatics Engineer at Children's Hospital of Philadelphia.

speakers.name: Kai-Hsun Chen
speakers.title: Hark
speakers.bio: Kai-Hsun leads infrastructure at Hark, spanning compute, data, and the full model lifecycle. Previously, he worked on infrastructure at xAI and Anyscale. He is also an open-source enthusiast who maintains several projects, including Ray, KubeRay, and Apache Submarine, and has been contributing actively to Kueue over the past few months.

speakers.name: Kanika Rana
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer @ Red Hat
speakers.bio: Kanika is a software engineer at Red Hat, where she has been contributing since 2021. She currently works on Argo CD as part of the GitOps team, focusing on scalable and reliable deployment workflows. Prior to this, she worked on the Developer Sandbox — a self-service platform for evaluating OpenShift.

speakers.name: Karena Angell
speakers.title: Senior Principal Technical Strategist, Global Engineering
speakers.bio: Karena Angell is a Senior Principal Technical Strategist, Global Engineering at Red Hat focusing on cloud native workloads for Kubernetes, open source software projects, agentic transformation and is the Chair of the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee.

speakers.name: Karim Alibhai
speakers.title: Staff Engineer @ AcuityMD
speakers.bio: Karim once ran a Kubernetes cluster from his basement and will find a way to bring it up in conversation. He loves building tools for other engineers, helping teams move faster, and writing that extra bit of code that makes someone's day. He's worked across infrastructure and application development, always with an eye for making software a pleasure to use. These days, he's obsessed with managing DuckDB on Kubernetes and playing Resident Evil. He considers both to be survival horror.

speakers.name: Karol Szuster
speakers.title: Software Engineer @ Google
speakers.bio: Software Engineer with 6+ years of experience. Previously built solutions for AI-driven data publication and curation. Currently at Google developing Kueue to enhance AI training and inference capabilities across Kubernetes clusters.

speakers.name: Karol Szwaj
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer @ Kubermatic
speakers.bio: Karol is a senior software engineer at Kubermatic, a maintainer of the Envoy Gateway and kube-bind projects, and is currently working on kcp. He specialises in open-source technologies, distributed systems, and networking, and brings a telecommunications background from university. Karol is an active contributor to the open-source ecosystem, with involvement in projects such as Kyma, Kubermatic, and several CNCF initiatives, including Istio, Envoy Gateway, Kube-OVN, kcp, and Kubernetes SIGs.

speakers.name: Karunasri Garigipati
speakers.title: Heroku (Lead Software Engineer)
speakers.bio: Karunasri(Karuna) Garigipati is a Lead Software Engineer at Heroku(Salesforce), working on Fir, Heroku’s Kubernetes-based platform. She started in observability, learning how platforms fail. Now she builds one, making the infrastructure that runs customer apps scalable, reliable, and secure. She also built Heroku’s AI-powered observability MCP server and wrote about it on the Heroku Engineering Blog. She has a photographic memory for faces. Unlike your logs, she has unlimited retention.

speakers.name: Kashif Khan
speakers.title: Maintainer, Open source Architect, PhD
speakers.bio: Kashif Khan is a co-chair of CNCF TAG Infrastructure and maintainer of the CNCF project Metal3.io for 6 years. He works as an open source Architect for Ericsson Software Technology, Finland. He holds a PhD in Computer Science. Kashif is a research and open source enthusiast and his current area of interest is kubernetes deployments on baremetal systems in distributed cloud scenarios.

speakers.name: Kaslin Fields
speakers.title: Google Developer Advocate
speakers.bio: Kaslin Fields is a Developer Advocate at Google Cloud, a Container enthusiast and creator of tech comics. She uses her knowledge of DevOps technologies and methodologies to help others as they enter the Cloud Native world. By creating comics about DevOps tech, she hopes to make learning Cloud Native fun and accessible to everyone!

speakers.name: Kasper Borg Nissen
speakers.title: Principal Developer Advocate at Dash0, former Co-Chair KubeCon+CloudNativeCon EU/NA, CNCF Ambassador, Golden Kubestronaut, KCD Organizer, Meet-up organizer
speakers.bio: Kasper is a CNCF Ambassador, former KubeCon+CloudNativeCon Co-Chair, Golden Kubestronaut, KCD Organizer, and CNCG Group Organizer. He co-founded Cloud Native Nordics to unite meetups across the region. At Dash0, he helps make observability easy for developers by advocating for better tooling, best practices, and seamless integrations. Bridging observability and platform engineering, he ensures developers stay productive and gain actionable insights exactly when needed.

speakers.name: Kat Cosgrove
speakers.title: Kubernetes Steering Committee | SIG Docs | SIG Release
speakers.bio: Kat is an open source advocate focused on the growth and nurturing of open source through authentic contribution. In particular, her specialties are approachable 101-level content and deep dives on the history of technology, with a focus on DevOps and cloud native. She was the Kubernetes Release Lead for 1.30 Uwubernetes, and currently serves as a member of the Kubernetes Steering Committee, the Release Team Subproject Lead, and a SIG Docs Tech Lead.

speakers.name: Kate Obiidykhata
speakers.title: Take the Complexity out of Going Cloud Native
speakers.bio: General manager for Cloud-Native Solutions with 11 years of experience across Linux security, open-source infrastructure, web hosting, and enterprise systems. Focused on supporting financial institutions, cloud providers, and multi-regional enterprises in adopting open-source platforms in production environments.

speakers.name: Kathan Kashiparekh
speakers.title: Senior Member of Technical Staff at Salesforce
speakers.bio: Senior software engineer at Salesforce building a robust and scalable Integration Testing platform while making it an easy and user friendly experience

speakers.name: Katherine Druckman
speakers.title: Open Source Evangelist, Intel
speakers.bio: Katherine Druckman is a senior technologist, speaker, and longtime advocate for open ecosystems. Currently Head of Community and Partnership Engagement at JetBrains, she specializes in developer experience, combining software ecosystem strategy, content strategy, and community building, grounded in a foundation of hands-on software engineering experience and proven leadership. She is a long-time open source advocate, developer, and podcaster, and is currently the host of the Reality2.0 podcast.

speakers.name: Kathryn Baldauf
speakers.title: Apple Containerization Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Kathryn is a software engineer at Apple, where she works on Apple's open source Container and Containerization projects. She has been working in the open source container ecosystem for the past 7 years.

speakers.name: Katie Meinders
speakers.title: Community, Isovalent @ Cisco
speakers.bio: Katie is a Community Outreach Manager at Isovalent @ Cisco who has spent nearly a decade in the cloud native community. She works closely with the Cilium and eBPF communities, focusing on the content and community engagement helping people discover and understand these projects and get involved.

speakers.name: Kavitha Daula
speakers.title: VP of Engineering, Edera
speakers.bio: Kavitha Daula is the VP of Engineering at Edera, where she leads the development of secure, high-performance container runtime technologies. Previously, she was Senior Director at GEICO, driving innovations in OS, containers, and language runtimes, including a custom Linux distro for secure workloads. With two decades of experience, she focuses on building developer-friendly platforms that balance strong isolation, performance, and usability.

speakers.name: Kaynan Coelho
speakers.title: Engineering Manager at Nubank
speakers.bio: Kaynan is a Brazilian Engineering Manager at Nubank, based in Fortaleza, Ceará. He leads teams responsible for large-scale data and observability platforms processing petabytes of telemetry data daily. His work focuses on engineering leadership and reliability at scale. At Observability Summit North America, Kaynan shares executive and technical insights from achieving an 8x reduction in query latency on Nubank’s internal logging platform.

speakers.name: Kazuki Sato
speakers.title: NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS, Inc.
speakers.bio: Kazuki Sato is a software engineer at NTT DOCOMO BUSINESS, Inc., specializing in cloud-native distributed systems and GPU infrastructure. He serves as Lead Architect for GoAT (GPU over APN Testbed), developing nationwide distributed AI platforms leveraging IOWN APN. He also holds a Maritime Officer license — making him one of the rare engineers who handles both physical and digital containers, at least in theory.

speakers.name: Keith Babo
speakers.title: Chief Product Officer - Solo.io
speakers.bio: Keith Babo is the Chief Product Officer at Solo.io, where he leads product strategy and execution, enabling enterprises to build and scale the next generation of cloud-native and agentic infrastructure for AI-driven applications. Prior to Solo.io, Keith held leadership roles in product management and engineering at Red Hat, Sun Microsystems, and Intel Corporation.

speakers.name: Keith Mattix
speakers.title: Senior Architect at Solo.io
speakers.bio: Keith is a Senior Architect at Solo.io serving as a lead on the Agentgateway project and a member of the Istio Technical Oversight Committee.

speakers.name: Kevin Dubois
speakers.title: Senior Principal Developer Advocate at IBM
speakers.bio: Kevin Dubois is often featured as a (keynote) speaker at conferences around the world, where he shares his passion and knowledge about developer experience, agentic AI, open source, cloud native development and Java. He is also an author, java Champion, and an accomplished software architect and platform engineer. Kevin currently works as a Senior Principal Developer Advocate at IBM, and is also Technical Lead for the CNCF Developer Experience Technical Advisory Group.

speakers.name: Kevin Hannon
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Red Hat
speakers.bio: Kevin Hannon is focused on improving AI/ML experience on Kubernetes. He started his career as a computational scientist and has always been interested in large scale batch jobs. He is motivated to improve Kubernetes in this area to benefit various use cases that are underserved by Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Kevin Klues
speakers.title: Distinguished Engineer at NVIDIA
speakers.bio: Kevin Klues is a distinguished engineer at NVIDIA. He is a former shadow member of the CNCF TOC and a sig-node maintainer, having helped design and implement the CPU, Device, and Topology Managers, Multi-Instance GPUs, and Dynamic Resource Allocation (DRA) in Kubernetes. Kevin holds a bachelors from Rose-Hulman Institute of Technology, a masters from Washington University in St. Louis, and a Ph.D. from UC Berkeley. When not working, you can find Kevin with his kids or enjoying a beer in the sun.

speakers.name: Kim Schaefer
speakers.title: Senior DevOps Engineer
speakers.bio:
