Kim Schaefer is a Senior DevOps and Cloud Engineer focused on Kubernetes, GitOps, and secure platform engineering. She designs and operates production Kubernetes platforms with a focus on deployment reliability and automation in constrained environments.

Kim's work centers on building GitOps platforms that teams can trust in production, especially where change must be deliberate and defensible. She is an open-source contributor and has previously spoken at Open Source Summit and GrafanaCON.

speakers.name: Krishna Rekapalli
speakers.title: Sr AI Engineer, IBM watsonx DataLabs
speakers.bio: Krishna Teja Rekapalli is a Sr AI Engineer at IBM watsonx DataLabs, specializing in enterprise LLM-powered AI and agentic workflows. With 7+ years in production ML, he has architected RAG systems across financial services, healthcare, and manufacturing. He works at the intersection of research and practice, with deep experience in the open-source AI ecosystem including Docling, OpenSearch, and K8s.

speakers.name: Kuba Tużnik
speakers.title: K8s SIG Autoscaling Lead | Senior Software Engineer @ Google
speakers.bio: Kuba is a Senior Software Engineer at Google. He has been maintaining Cluster Autoscaler since 2019, and took on the position of Kubernetes SIG Autoscaling co-chair in 2025. Within the SIG, Kuba's main area of expertise is Node autoscaling.

speakers.name: Lachlan Evenson
speakers.title: Principal Product Manager - Cloud Native Ecosystem
speakers.bio: Lachlan is a Principal Program Manager on the open source team at Azure. As an emeritus Kubernetes steering committee member and release lead, Lachlan has deep operational knowledge of many Cloud Native projects. He spends his days building and contributing to software that addresses key challenges in the Cloud Native ecosystem. @LachlanEvenson

speakers.name: Lakmal Warusawithana
speakers.title: Maintainer of OpenChoreo
speakers.bio: Lakmal Warusawithana is a maintainer of OpenChoreo, a CNCF Sandbox project, and a Distinguished Engineer at WSO2. He has led the design of scalable cloud-native developer platforms for enterprises. Previously, he served as VP of the Apache Stratos PaaS project and co-founded thinkCube, where he helped build cloud platforms for telecom operators. Lakmal is a frequent speaker at industry conferences on Kubernetes, platform engineering, and cloud-native architectures.

speakers.name: Lasse Vierow
speakers.title: Cloud Engineer
speakers.bio: Spent the last few years working in cloud engineering and enjoy cloud native. Participated in the Linux Foundation Mentorship Program and like to explore new technologies, sharing ideas, and connecting with people from around the world.

speakers.name: Laura Lorenz
speakers.title: SWE at Google
speakers.bio: Laura Lorenz is a software engineer at Google. She is an active member of Kubernetes’ upstream focused on SIG-Multicluster, SIG-Node, and releases.

speakers.name: Laura Luttmer
speakers.title: Product at Bindplane (Dynatrace)
speakers.bio: Laura Luttmer is a Product Manager at Bindplane, an OpenTelemetry-native pipeline management platform. She has over 10 years of product experience spanning SaaS, legal, and data platforms, and currently focuses on the tooling and patterns that help teams get more out of their observability data.

speakers.name: Lebin Cheng
speakers.title: RailXia, Founder and CEO
speakers.bio:
Serial entrepreneur with multiple successful exits: cofounder of Netskope (IPO) and cofounder of CloudVector(acquired by Imperva/Thales). 
Proven track record of building companies to deliver first in class solutions to meet emerging security needs of enterprise customers. 
Over 20 years in the field of cyber security. Proven track record of working with open source communities.

speakers.name: Lee Calcote
speakers.title: Founder, Layer5
speakers.bio: Lee Calcote is an innovative product and technology leader, passionate about empowering engineers and enabling organizations. As Founder of Layer5, he is at the forefront of the cloud native movement. Open source, advanced and emerging technologies have been a consistent focus through Calcote’s tenure at SolarWinds, Seagate, Cisco and Schneider Electric. An advisor, author, and speaker, Calcote is active in the community as a Docker Captain, Cloud Native Ambassador and Google SoC Mentor.

speakers.name: Leigh Capili
speakers.title: Flux Maintainer, Principal Consultant - ControlPlane
speakers.bio:
Leigh is an empathetic speaker and developer with niches in cloud-native systems and security. He has a background in building software to manage infrastructure.

Leigh authored kubeadm’s etcd mTLS implementation and Flux 2’s multi-tenant security model.

Leigh worked with the VMware Tanzu Advocacy team and previously built Developer Experience and Platform with Weaveworks, Beatport, AT&T, and DIRECTV.

Leigh and his wife enjoy snowboarding and have a 60lb dog named Pepsi.

speakers.name: Léonard Suslian
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Compute Infrastructure - Mistral AI
speakers.bio: I build infrastructure services for bare-metal GPU kubernetes clusters.

speakers.name: Leonardo Grasso
speakers.title: Falco Core Maintainer
speakers.bio: Based in Sicily, Leonardo is passionate about R&D, software design, and building open source tools that engineers enjoy using. He has been working in security by accident since 2020 and is a Falco Core Maintainer. He also leads Sysdig’s open source team, overseeing its work on Falco and Wireshark.

speakers.name: Lev Andelman
speakers.title: CTO @ Terasky, ortholinear keyboard builder
speakers.bio: I am a Linux sysadmin that woke up one morning to a world of DevOps. I was lucky to be part of small companies that grew to a huge scale through insane outages. Those outages took my sleep but awarded me with experience. Today I am Hashicorp Ambassador, Israel Hashicorp User Group co-organizer, DevOpsDays Tel Aviv co-organizer and CTO at cloud and devops consulting company.

speakers.name: Lin Sun
speakers.title: solo.io
speakers.bio: Lin is the Head of Open Source at Solo.io, contributing full-time to the open-source community. She serves on the CNCF Technical Oversight Committee (TOC), is a CNCF Ambassador, and is a maintainer for Istio, kgateway, and kagent. An international speaker at tech conferences, Lin frequently blogs about gateways, service meshes, cloud-native connectivity, and AI agents. She is the author of “Sidecar-less Istio Explained” and “AI Agents in Kubernetes”, and holds more than 200 patents.

speakers.name: Lior Lieberman
speakers.title: Senior Engineering Lead, Google
speakers.bio: Lior is an engineering lead at Google working on Google Compute Engine and Cloud Service Mesh. He is a leading maintainer of ingress2gateway, and an active contributor to Kubernetes SIG network focused on Gateway API.

speakers.name: Liqian Luo
speakers.title: Partner Software Engineering Manager - Microsoft
speakers.bio: Liqian Luo is a Partner Software Engineering Manager at Microsoft, where she leads the advanced services on top of vanilla Kubernetes: multi-cluster management to manage clusters at scale, AKS Automatic to simplify cluster operations, and most recently, AI infra on Kubernetes. Prior to working at Microsoft, she built various large scale data services including cloud asset inventory, cloud tracing, friend recommendations, just to name a few, at Google.

speakers.name: Liudmila Molkova
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Google, Member of the OpenTelemetry Technical Committee
speakers.bio: Liudmila Molkova is a Software Engineer at Google working on OpenTelemetry. She is a member of the OpenTelemetry Technical Committee and a maintainer of the Semantic Conventions. Previously, she led observability efforts for Azure client libraries at Microsoft. Liudmila co-authored distributed tracing implementations across the .NET ecosystem, including HTTP client instrumentation and Azure Functions.

speakers.name: Liz Rice
speakers.title: Chief Open Source Officer, Isovalent @ Cisco
speakers.bio:
Liz Rice is Chief Open Source Officer at Isovalent, now part of Cisco. She is an award-winning speaker, and author of O'Reilly books on "Container Security" and "Learning eBPF". She represents Maintainers on the CNCF governing board, and was previously chair of the Technical Oversight Committee, Co-Chair of KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, and on the board of OpenUK.

Liz loves riding bikes in places with better weather than her native London, and making music under the pseudonym Insider Nine.

speakers.name: Logan Koch
speakers.title: Software Engineer - BondVRS
speakers.bio: Software Engineer with over 15 years experience. Co-leads Merge Forward's Friends of Dorothy working group. Active member of the Deaf and Hard of Hearing working group.

speakers.name: Long Nguyen
speakers.title: ML Engineer at The Philadelphia Phillies
speakers.bio: Long Nguyen is a Machine Learning Engineer at the Philadelphia Phillies. He started his career as a quantitative analyst building predictive and generative models to aid in-game strategies. Today, he’s developing framework and toolings to manage and deploy model pipelines at scale.

speakers.name: Lorenzo Biava
speakers.title: Staff Infrastructure Engineer, LiveKit
speakers.bio: Lorenzo Biava a Staff Infrastructure Engineer at LiveKit, where he operates a global WebRTC network pushing over 10 PB of monthly real-time traffic across dozens of regions. He previously served as Principal Engineer at Microsoft and Nuance, building secure, globally-distributed Kubernetes platforms for Voice AI in strictly regulated environments.

speakers.name: Lu Zhang
speakers.title: Member of Technical Staff, LLM Inference, OpenAI
speakers.bio: Lu Zhang is an engineer at OpenAI focused on large-scale AI infrastructure. He currently works on inference systems and previously helped build and operate GPU clusters on OpenAI's Fleet team. His interests span Kubernetes, cloud-native platforms, distributed systems, reliability engineering, and machine learning infrastructure. He is passionate about scaling infrastructure for AI workloads and enabling reliable, efficient operation of GPU-accelerated clusters in production.

speakers.name: Lucas Fernandes Martins
speakers.title: Mistral AI, Inference Software Engineer
speakers.bio: I'm a software engineer at Mistral working on Inference.

speakers.name: Lucas Käldström
speakers.title: Kubernetes & Cloud Native Developer and Speaker
speakers.bio: Lucas is a Kubernetes and cloud native contributor since 10 years. He was a CNCF Ambassador for 7 years, awarded Top CNCF Ambassador 2017 with Sarah Novotny. Lucas was a co-lead for SIG Cluster Lifecycle, co-created kubeadm, and ported Kubernetes to ARM. Lucas has been running meetups and KCD Helsinki in Finland, co-created the meetup collective Cloud Native Nordics and has spoken at 10 KubeCons. Lucas is now researching control plane access control as a Staff Software Engineer at Upbound.

speakers.name: Lucy Sweet
speakers.title: Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic
speakers.bio: Lucy is a Member of Technical Staff at Anthropic and co-lead of the Kubernetes Node Lifecycle Working Group.

speakers.name: Luiz Scheidegger
speakers.title: Member of Technical Staff, Anthropic
speakers.bio: Luiz is an engineer at Anthropic on the Claude Managed Agents team, building the sandboxing infrastructure that runs Claude agents. Before that he was Head of Engineering at Lindy.ai and an engineer at Nextdoor, where he built Launch Control, the company’s experimentation platform. Earlier he worked at Facebook and Uber.

speakers.name: Lukasz Ciukaj
speakers.title: Observability Solutions Architect, Cisco Splunk | OpenTelemetry Enthusiast | Cloud Native RTP Community Organizer (part of CNCF)
speakers.bio: With over 10 years of industry experience, Lukasz initially specialized in networking but four years ago, he transitioned into software, cloud technologies, and applications world, with a particular interest in Observability. He has gained valuable expertise in tools like AppDynamics, ThousandEyes, Splunk, and OpenTelemetry, enhancing his technical skill set. He enjoys sharing his knowledge with others on multiple platforms, including blog articles on Splunk.com and LinkedIn posts.

speakers.name: Maciej Szulik
speakers.title: Defense Unicorns, Staff Platform Engineer
speakers.bio: Maciej has spent more than 20 years building software and hasn't lost his curiosity yet. By day, he’s tackling Kubernetes challenges for Defense Unicorns. By night, he’s a Python tinkerer working on side projects. A firm believer in the "always be learning" mindset, he balances his technical life with a love for photography and a deep stack of books.

speakers.name: Maciej Wal
speakers.title: Cybersecurity Platform Architect, The Cybersecurity Center at MSU Denver
speakers.bio: Maciej Wal is a Cybersecurity Platform Architect at the Cybersecurity Center at MSU Denver, where he designs and operates a cloud-native SOC platform serving multiple community partners across rural Colorado on a $1,000/month budget. He trains student engineers who now maintain the platform in production, and has placed graduates into DevOps and security roles across industry. His work spans GitOps, zero-trust architecture, and observability.

speakers.name: Maciek Różacki
speakers.title: Google, Group Product Manager
speakers.bio: Product manager behind K8Ss and GKEs capabilities for Scalability, HPC, Batch and AI Training use cases. Figuring out how to make Kubernetes a the best platform to build research platforms.

speakers.name: Maia Iyer
speakers.title: IBM Research
speakers.bio: Maia is an Advisory Software Engineer at IBM Research specializing in platform engineering and cloud-native security. While deeply experienced in zero trust - a dedicated maintainer of SPIFFE's Tornjak project - her research now tackles the infrastructure demands of the AI era. An active and passionate speaker and blogger, Maia now explores the intersection of agentic workloads and Kubernetes, and how cloud-native platforms must evolve to make AI agents run reliably and securely.

speakers.name: Manabu McCloskey
speakers.title: Sr. Solutions Architect at AWS
speakers.bio: Manabu is a Solutions Architect at Amazon Web Services. He focuses on contributing to open source application delivery tooling and works with AWS strategic customers to design and implement enterprise solutions using AWS resources and open source technologies. His interests include Kubernetes, GitOps, Serverless, and Souls Series.

speakers.name: Manfred Moser
speakers.title: Open source coder, mentor, educator, and advocate
speakers.bio: Manfred Moser is a Senior Principal DevRel Engineer at Chainguard, bringing a profound focus on software supply chain security to the open source world. A dedicated community leader and published author, he brings decades of technical expertise as a software engineer and advocate. He has a deep, influential history with the Apache Maven ecosystem, including authoring prominent reference books, and is an active Trino maintainer, advocate, and podcast host.

speakers.name: Marcin Wielgus
speakers.title: Staff Software Engineer @ Google
speakers.bio: Marcin Wielgus is a Staff Software Engineer at Google. Marcin joined the company in 2010 and since then he has been working on various projects, ranging from Android applications to recommendation engines. He started contributing to Kubernetes before the 1.0 release and currently leads the K8S batch team at Google.

speakers.name: Marco Martinez
speakers.title: Community Team Lead, Coder
speakers.bio: I lead community strategy at Coder, building programs that connect developers, open source users, and the business. My path into community is a little unconventional, with a background spanning video games, social, video, paid media, SEO, and content. Today, I bring those experiences together to grow community, strengthen product feedback loops, and show how community can drive adoption and business impact.

speakers.name: Marcos Hernández
speakers.title: Distinguished Engineer
speakers.bio: Marcos is a Distinguished Engineer with Isovalent@Cisco and works on Kubernetes NEtworking and Datacenter networking solutions and products

speakers.name: Marek Pelka
speakers.title: Engineering Manager at monday.com
speakers.bio: Marek Pelka is an engineering manager at monday.com, where he leads platform engineering initiatives, including the company's internal developer portal. Based in Warsaw, Poland, Marek focuses on developer experience and infrastructure tooling at scale.

speakers.name: Marek Siarkowicz
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer, Google
speakers.bio: Marek is a Staff Software Engineer at Google, SIG-etcd tech lead, approver in API machinery, and contributor to Kubernetes scalability. He began his career at Warsaw startups, where he developed a passion for open source and extreme programming

speakers.name: Marino Wijay
speakers.title: Engineered Solutions - Networking, APIs, Kubernetes, AI
speakers.bio: Marino Wijay is a Canadian, Traveller, International Speaker, and Open Source Advocate and Architect for AI, API Platforms, Service Mesh, Kubernetes, and Networking. He is a CNCF Ambassador,  Organizer for KCD Toronto, and Founder of EmpathyOps. He is passionate about technology and modern distributed systems. He will always fall back to the patterns of Networking and the ways of the OSI. Community building is his driving force; A modern Jedi Academy.

speakers.name: Mariusz Sabath
speakers.title: Senior Technical Staff Member in IBM Research
speakers.bio: Mr. Sabath is a Senior Technical Staff Member on the AI Platforms team at IBM Research, with extensive experience and a long track record in cloud-native security. He is Project Lead for Kagenti, an open-source Kubernetes platform for AI agents, a SPIFFE Steering Committee member, and manages IBM's open source contribution process. His work focuses on Zero Trust for agentic workloads—workload identity, authorization, and secure tool access. He holds nearly 30 patents.

speakers.name: Mark Rossetti
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Microsoft
speakers.bio:
Mark Rossetti is a software engineering focusing on open-source projects at Microsoft and is also the co-chair of Kubernetes' SIG-Windows. 
Mark focuses on improving the experience of using Windows containers in Kubernetes. 
Mark has also served on the Kubernetes release team since v1.25 and was the Enhancements Lead for v1.27

speakers.name: Marlow Warnicke
speakers.title: Principal Cloud Engineer at NVIDIA
speakers.bio: Marlow is a Senior Engineer at NVIDIA and a chair for CNCF TAG Workloads and the CNCF Batch Subproject. Marlow has expertise in resource management, the AI/ML Kubernetes cloud compute ecosystem, embedded systems, high performance compute system tools, kernel drivers, tracing libraries, and security. Marlow's interests lie in optimizing the cloud native ecosystem for both heterogeneous systems and also for HPC/AI/ML compute with an eye for both performance and efficiency.

speakers.name: Marly Salazar
speakers.title: Maintainer
speakers.bio: I am a software engineer with a heavy background in legacy and on premises systems, and migrating those to the cloud, modernizing and automating them. I have been working on the kubernetes project for a year and a half, primarily on kubectl.

speakers.name: Maroon Ayoub
speakers.title: Senior Principal Machine Learning Engineer, Red Hat
speakers.bio: Maroon Ayoub is an AI infrastructure architect at Red Hat focused on distributed inference. He co-leads development of llm-d and specializes in scaling LLM inference with Kubernetes-native architectures, KV-cache orchestration, and open source integrations.

speakers.name: Mary Campbell
speakers.title: Linux Foundation Education, Sr. Manager Education Solutions
speakers.bio: With more than 30 years of experience in technical services and account management, Mary helps organizations worldwide using open source software to create new opportunities, products, and experiences. The Linux Foundation offers flexible training, rigorous certifications, and engagement options for varied needs and budgets. Its expanding education portfolio supports Linux, cloud native, security, decentralized trust, AI, networking, and other high-demand technology fields.

speakers.name: Masato Kozuka
speakers.title: Hitachi, Ltd., Member of Technical Staff,  Platform Engineering & Security Specialist
speakers.bio: Masato Kozuka is a Platform Engineering and Security specialist at Hitachi, Ltd., where he leads architecture for the company's enterprise AI agent platform enforcing least-privilege access across diverse clients, agents, and users. He is also a Backstage organization member, plugin maintainer, and Keycloak contributor whose Backstage plugin abstracts Keycloak OIDC integration for platform teams. He brings the same philosophy to this session: make secure-by-default access a platform primitive.

speakers.name: Mathew Wicks
speakers.title: Open Source Developer Relations @ NVIDIA | Kubeflow Maintainer
speakers.bio:
At NVIDIA, Mathew works with critical open-source projects and their maintainers to enable success on current and future NVIDIA platforms.

Independantly, Mathew serves on the Kubeflow Steering Committee and leads the development of the Kubeflow Notebooks sub-project.

speakers.name: Mathis Felardos
speakers.title: Mistral AI, Inference Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Mathis Felardos is an Inference Software Developer at Mistral AI for the past two years, with a main focus on Disaggregated Serving and other infrastructure-based optimizations for LLMs. He is a maintainer of the LeaderWorkerSet and DisaggregatedSet projects.

speakers.name: Matt Boersma
speakers.title: Senior SWE, Microsoft
speakers.bio: Matt has worked with software systems since the 1980s in a variety of capacities, focusing recently on cloud and container technologies.

speakers.name: Matt Dering
speakers.title: ML Engineer At The Philadelphia Phillies
speakers.bio: Matt Dering, PhD is a Machine Learning Engineer in the Philadelphia Phillies R&D department. Prior to that he got his PhD in Computer Science at Penn State in 2018, specializing in Machine Learning in Engineering Design.

speakers.name: Matt Farina
speakers.title: Head of Portfolio Architecture and Community
speakers.bio: Matt works as Head of Portfolio Architecture and Community at SUSE. He is a maintainer on Helm and Artifact Hub. Matt is an author, speaker, and regular contributor to open source.

speakers.name: Matt Heon
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Red Hat
speakers.bio: Matt is one of the core maintainers of Podman and leads the team working on Podman, Buildah, and Skopeo at Red Hat. He's worked on Podman since the project's inception. In his off time, he enjoys baking and reading.

speakers.name: Matt Lord
speakers.title: Vitess Maintainer @ PlanetScale
speakers.bio: Matt Lord has spent the last 25+ years working in the database space both as a producer at MySQL and MongoDB and as a consumer at WeWork and Etsy. Today he leverages these decades of experience to help make Vitess the best Open Source solution for running MySQL at scale and supporting the PlanetScale team as we revolutionize the database developer experience.

speakers.name: Matt Matejczyk
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Google
speakers.bio: Matt is a Software Engineer at Google, working on GKE and Kubernetes. He also serves as the chair of the Workload Aware Scheduling Working Group (WG-WAS).

speakers.name: Maxime Coquerel
speakers.title: Director | Principal Cloud Security Architect | CNCF Ambassador | Microsoft MVP Azure & Cloud Security
speakers.bio:
In my current role at Royal Bank of Canada (RBC), I lead the Kubernetes Security program, overseeing security architecture, cloud threat research, threat modeling, and risk assessment of cloud designs and patterns. 

Additionally, I collaborate closely with our strategic partners, cultivating and sustaining business relationships with third-party providers, including cloud vendor teams and emerging cloud security startups.

speakers.name: Medya Ghazizadeh
speakers.title: Technical lead at Google
speakers.bio: Master of computer science from DePaul University in Chicago,  minikube maintainer since 2019 and author of multiple open source projects and 6K contributors to Kubernetes (top 25 all time)

speakers.name: Mengjin Yan
speakers.title: Tech Lead Manager at Anyscale
speakers.bio: Mengjin Yan is a Ray committer and engineering lead for Ray Core at Anyscale, where she helps shape the evolution of Ray’s foundation layer. Her work includes task event infrastructure, label-based and topology-aware scheduling, and improvements to Ray Core’s scheduling and observability. Before Anyscale, she spent seven years at LinkedIn building large-scale online storage and distributed database systems.

speakers.name: Mengxuan Li
speakers.title: Dynamia.ai
speakers.bio:
Maintainer of HAMi community
Approver of volcano community

Responsible for the development of gpu virtualization mechanism on HAMi and volcano. Working on providing device-sharing on all heterogeneous devices and improving device utilization on clusters.

speakers.name: Mert Toslali
speakers.title: Staff Research Scientist, IBM Research
speakers.bio: Mert Toslali is a Staff Research Scientist at IBM Research, where he focuses on optimizing training and inference pipelines for generative AI at scale. He holds a Ph.D. from Boston University and works at the intersection of systems and AI. He brings a deep background in systems research for platform engineering and is an experienced speaker, having presented his work at venues such as MLSys, SoCC, the PyTorch Conference, and other leading technical venues.

speakers.name: Mesut Oezdil
speakers.title: DevOps Engineer
speakers.bio: Mesut Özdil is a DevOps engineer based in Germany and the Tech Lead of CNCF’s TAG Infrastructure. He holds the CKA, CKS, and CDP certifications, is a Nebius AI CloudOps Engineer, and was selected for Nebius’s inaugural Fellowship cohort. His work spans Kubernetes infrastructure, GPU virtualization, and observability. He is a core contributor to Project HAMi, a CNCF Sandbox project bringing GPU sharing and overcommit protection to Kubernetes, and contributes to the open source projects.

speakers.name: Micah Hausler
speakers.title: Principal Engineer, AWS
speakers.bio: Micah is a Principal Engineer at AWS, focused on Amazon EKS and Kubernetes security

speakers.name: Michael Amundson
speakers.title: Distinguished Engineer, CVS Health
speakers.bio: Michael Amundson is a distinguished engineer in the Developer Experience organization at CVS Health where he leads technical direction for the CAP Application Platform. His near decade of experience in platform engineering started at Target Corporation, where he helped build Target's in-house application platform. Prior to his work on platforms, Michael worked as an application engineer in roles across a number of Fortune 500 companies, daydreaming of platforms that didn't yet exist.

speakers.name: Michael Aspinwall
speakers.title: Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Michael is a software engineer at Google and has been contributing to Kubernetes, DRANet and other OSS initiatives. His background consists of Kubernetes, Networking, and has been working in the field as both a consumer of Kubernetes and maintainer. His primary focus as of present is Scalability and how to push Kubernetes past its current limits.

speakers.name: Michael Bolot
speakers.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer at GEICO
speakers.bio: Michael has worked for the last four years in the Kubernetes Ecosystem. He currently works on multi-cloud compute and networking at GEICO and previously worked at SUSE on Rancher (specializing in RBAC, API Frameworks, and Virtual Clusters).

speakers.name: Michael Crenshaw
speakers.title: Senior Staff Software Engineer, Intuit
speakers.bio: Michael Crenshaw is a Staff Software Engineer on the Argo CD team at Intuit. He is the most active contributor to the Argo project, focusing on security and performance improvements in Argo CD. He helps maintain Intuit’s ~50 Argo CD instances and ~20k Argo CD applications.

speakers.name: Michael Friese
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft
speakers.bio: Michael is a Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft, specializing in Kubernetes, containers, eBPF, networking, and security. He is currently contributing to Inspektor Gadget, an open-source observability, security and debugging tool under the CNCF.

speakers.name: Michael Irwin
speakers.title: DevRel at Docker
speakers.bio:
Michael Irwin has been a developer for ~20 years and a part of the container space since 2016. He's passionate about making development easier for all and breaking down complex concepts into simpler ideas. 

He previously worked in the university setting for 11 years and has been on Docker's DevRel team for ~4.5 years. He loves educating, pushing boundaries, and learning from others.

Outside of work, you'll find him spending time with his family of eight kids or trying to enjoy the outdoors.

speakers.name: Michael Kinsley
speakers.title: Hybrid Cloud Fabric - Agent of Chaos
speakers.bio: Michael Kinsley is Director of GEICO's Hybrid Cloud Fabric, a multi-provider zero-trust platform based on Istio, Cilium, and SPIFFE/SPIRE. He set the vision and hired the team that built it. His dream was always an org that gives back to the community, not just one that consumes it, and he's finally living it.

speakers.name: Michael Levan
speakers.title: Building High-Performing Agentic and Kubernetes Environments | AI Architect | CNCF Ambassador | 4x Published Author & International Public Speaker
speakers.bio: Michael Levan translates technical complexity into practical value. He is an AI Architect, solutions engineer, and content creator in the AI and Platform Engineering space who spends his time working with organizations around the globe on technical implementation and strategy. Michael is also a Microsoft MVP, 4x published author, podcast host, international public speaker, CNCF Ambassador, and was part of the Kubernetes v1.28 and v1.31 Release Team.

speakers.name: Michael McCune
speakers.title: Software Engineer @ Red Hat
speakers.bio: Michael McCune is a software developer creating open source infrastructure and applications for cloud platforms. He has a passion for problem solving and team building, and a lifelong love of music, food, and culture.

speakers.name: Michael Zazula
speakers.title: Lead Machine Learning Engineer @ Capital One
speakers.bio: Mike is an engineer on the ML tooling team within Capital One. His primary focus is on building reusable tools and components across the Machine Learning Development Lifecycle for Data Scientists within the Org. Mike lives in New Jersey with his wife. Outside of work, his hobbies include home renovations (electrical, plumbing, tiling, etc.), gardening, and most recently has taken up beekeeping.

speakers.name: Michael Rishi Forrester
speakers.title: Preparing Tomorrow's Innovators, Elevating the Average
speakers.bio: Michael Forrester is a student, explorer, and educator at the boundary between humanity and technology. Over 25+ years he's gone from CTO to IC across operations, AI, cloud, and platform engineering, including time at AWS, ThoughtWorks, Red Hat, and Honeywell. His training has reached over a million engineers. He speaks at KubeCon and CNCF on Claude Code, MCP, and AI safety for platform engineers. Tools don't transform organizations. People do.

speakers.name: Michas Szacillo
speakers.title: Senior Engineer @ Bloomberg
speakers.bio: Michas is the Engineering Team Lead of Bloomberg’s Streaming Platform. The platform, which is running on Kubernetes, serves as the foundation for many of Bloomberg's data streaming use cases. Michas is also a frequent collaborator to the CNCF community, with contributions to projects including Karmada and KServe. He currently serves as a core maintainer of Karmada.

speakers.name: Micheal Kingston
speakers.title: Solutions Architect, NGINX/F5
speakers.bio: Micheal Kingston is a Product Manager at F5 who works on NGINX projects that help users manage application traffic in Kubernetes environments. He drives projects NGINX Ingress Controller and NGINX Gateway Fabric. Micheal was previously a software developer and DevOps engineer, and he spent several years working as a solutions architect for NGINX. He has a strong interest in modern applications, Kubernetes, and cloud-native technologies.

speakers.name: Michele Mancioppi
speakers.title: I am a man of simple tastes: I like my software boring, and my observability easy and powerful.
speakers.bio: Michele has active in the observability space for more than a decade. Former staff engineer turned PM and then back, he likes to code tracing instrumentation, Kubernetes operators and Infrastructure-as-Code integrations for observability almost as much as asking "Why would you need that?".

speakers.name: Michelle Au
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Google
speakers.bio: Michelle Au is a software engineer at Google and is a Kubernetes SIG Storage tech lead. She has been a Kubernetes maintainer since 2018,  working on projects including the Container Storage Interface, volume security, volume topology, and local persistent storage.

speakers.name: Mickey Boxell
speakers.title: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure
speakers.bio: Mickey Boxell is a Lead Principal Product Manager in the Containers and Kubernetes Services group within Oracle Cloud Infrastructure. He has been a member of the Kubernetes release team for many releases, including as the communications coordinator and docs lead. Mickey has worked in the cloud platform and infrastructure space for the past decade. In his spare time, you can find him biking, climbing, or taking care of a perilously large number of plants at his home in Southern California.

speakers.name: Mike Dame
speakers.title: Odigos
speakers.bio: Software engineer working on OpenTelemetry and Kubernetes

speakers.name: Mike Morris
speakers.title: Senior Product Manager, Microsoft
speakers.bio: Mike is a product manager at Microsoft working on upstream open source projects with a focus on Istio service mesh, and a Gateway API for service mesh co-lead. He is interested in building healthy, sustainable communities and scalable distributed systems, and working collaboratively to drive positive change.

speakers.name: Mike Shi
speakers.title: Head of Product, Observability
speakers.bio: Mike leads observability at ClickHouse, where he works on ClickStack, a developer-focused observability platform. He joined ClickHouse through the acquisition of HyperDX, a company he co-founded, after spending five years building tools for engineers and gradually becoming a database person along the way. Now, he focuses on improving open-source observability tooling, from polishing buttons and docs to optimizing search and ingestion infrastructure.

speakers.name: Mike Stefaniak
speakers.title: Senior Manager, Product, AWS
speakers.bio: Mike Stefaniak is a Senior Manager of Product at AWS, where he leads product strategy for containers. His team focuses on simplifying Kubernetes for platform engineers and application developers at scale, spanning compute elasticity, workload abstraction, and cluster governance.

speakers.name: Mike Wilson
speakers.title: Principal Architect, Adobe Inc
speakers.bio: Mike Wilson is a Principal Architect at Adobe, leading a 200,000+ virtual-core migration onto OpenShift and advising GPU and LLM-inference strategy. The through-line of his career is placement and scheduling at scale — from one of the largest OpenStack deployments in production (~20,000 nodes) and the Nova scheduler upstream, to GPU placement today. He lives in Alpine, Utah, trains Brazilian jiu-jitsu, and reads widely across theology, philosophy, and geopolitics.

speakers.name: Mitch Connors
speakers.title: Sr. Principal Engineer, Aviatrix
speakers.bio: Mitch Connors is a Principal Software Engineer at Microsoft, and serves on the Istio Technical Oversight Committee. Over the past 17 years, Mitch has worked at Google, F5 Networks, Amazon, an Industrial IoT startup, and State Farm Insurance, giving him a broad perspective on the needs of Enterprise Software Developers. This experience has given Mitch a passion for bringing technological innovation to the long tail of technology adopters without the need to start from scratch.

speakers.name: Mofesola Babalola
speakers.title: Staff Site Reliability Engineer, Tempo
speakers.bio: Mofesola Babalola is a Site Reliability Engineering leader at Tempo Software, managing observability and service mesh systems for over 5 million users. Expert in Kubernetes, Istio, ArgoCD, and Flux, he specializes in resilient platforms and automation. Mofesola has led production ambient mesh adoption and GitOps workflows, sharing practical insights at the intersection of DevOps, SRE, and developer experience.

speakers.name: Mofi Rahman
speakers.title: Developer Relations Engineer, Google
speakers.bio:
Mofi Rahman (@moficodes) is a Developer Advocate at Google. His favorite programming language these days is Go. He is a strong believer of the power of open source and importance of giving back to the community. He is a self proclaimed sticker collecting addict and has collected several box full of stickers with no signs of stopping. He can talk about TTRPGs for days.

He creates short tech videos on https://youtube.com/@ContainerBytes where covers various cloud native technologies.

speakers.name: Mohan Boddu
speakers.title: Engineering Manager at Red Hat
speakers.bio:
Open Source Enthusiast
Fedora Contributor
Community Manager for Podman Container Tools Project.

speakers.name: Morten Jæger Torkildsen
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer, Google
speakers.bio: Morten Jæger Torkildsen is a software engineer on the GKE/Kubernetes team at Google. He contributes to OSS Kubernetes and other projects in the Kubernetes ecosystem.

speakers.name: Moshiur Rahman
speakers.title: Ericsson Software Technology, Experienced Cloud Developer
speakers.bio: Open source contributor and maintainer with 6+ years of experience working on CNCF ecosystem projects. Maintainer of Metal3 project, with strong expertise in Kubernetes, Cluster API, and infrastructure automation. Active contributor to multiple open source projects including CAPO (Cluster API Provider OpenStack), focusing on bare metal provisioning, cloud-native infrastructure and platform engineering.

speakers.name: Mrunal Patel
speakers.title: Distinguished Engineer, Red Hat
speakers.bio: Mrunal Patel is a Distinguished Engineer at Red Hat working on Kubernetes for Openshift. He is a maintainer of runc/libcontainer and the OCI runtime specification. He started the CRI-O runtime. He is a SIG-Node chair and tech lead.

speakers.name: Muhammed Yunas Chirayath
speakers.title: Best Buy, Principle Site Reliability Engineer
speakers.bio: Muhammed Yunas Chirayath is a Site Reliability Engineer with production experience building and operating large-scale platforms on OpenShift and Kubernetes. He specializes in observability strategy, cost optimization, and platform reliability. He has led efforts to build unified observability platforms, reduce telemetry waste, and solve hard networking and reliability problems that rarely make it into documentation but always show up in production.

speakers.name: Nabarun Pal
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineer at Broadcom, Kubernetes Maintainer
speakers.bio: Nabarun is a Principal Software Engineer at Broadcom, a maintainer of the Kubernetes project, an emeritus member of the Kubernetes Steering Committee member and a chair of Kubernetes SIG Contributor Experience. He is a Release Manager for Kubernetes and has been the Kubernetes 1.21 Release Team Lead. Nabarun continuously mentors newcomers in the community through various means. He has been featured multiple times in Times of India and other publications for his open source work.

speakers.name: Naoki Oguchi
speakers.title: Director, Fsas Technologies Inc.
speakers.bio: Naoki Oguchi is responsible for development of infrastructure software, especially developing future technologies in Linux and Kubernetes. He has been with Fujitsu since 1992, working on communication software development including Frame Relay/ATM switch, IP router, Firewall, LTE/WiMAX wireless system, WAN acceleration technique, SDN, NFV and Data center network. He has obtained a Ph.D. degree in informatics. He also co-chaired the KubeDay Japan 2022.

speakers.name: Natali Vlatko
speakers.title: Director of Open Source Software Engineering at Cisco, SIG Docs Co-Chair for Kubernetes
speakers.bio: Natali Vlatko (she/her) is a Director of Open Source Software Engineering at Cisco, specializing in open software, policy, and governance. She is a SIG Docs Co-Chair for Kubernetes and a member of the TODO Group Steering Committee. She plays on the fun computer in her spare time. Her academic background is in Egyptology and Archaeology; specifically, burial customs across the various kingdoms of Ancient Egypt. Ask her about dead stuff.

speakers.name: Natalie Bandel
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer, Cloud Computing, NVIDIA
speakers.bio: Natalie is a Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA. She works on building software for cloud infrastructure powered by Kubernetes, KubeVirt and strong coffee.

speakers.name: Natalie Fisher
speakers.title: Principal Cloud Native Strategist & Ecosystem Lead
speakers.bio: Natalie Fisher is a Principal Cloud Native Strategist and Ecosystem lead for VMware Cloud Foundation at Broadcom. She drives VMware's cloud-native strategy, working across engineering, product, and the CNCF community to drive Kubernetes adoption, technical positioning, and developer engagement. A frequent speaker and blogger, Natalie is passionate about open source, platform engineering, and helping enterprises succeed with Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Nathan Herz
speakers.title: Software Engineer at NVIDIA
speakers.bio: Nathan Herz works as a software engineer on DGX Cloud at NVIDIA. Nathan's team is responsible for GPU node  health across all major cloud providers. He is also a member of the Kubernetes Security Response Committee.

speakers.name: Nathan Wood
speakers.title: “It was on fire when I got here”

speakers.name: Navjot Singh
speakers.title: Machine Learning Engineer, Shopify
speakers.bio: Navjot Singh is a recent graduate of the University of Waterloo, where he earned a Bachelor's degree in Mathematics. He is currently an Applied Machine Learning Engineer at Shopify, working on Sidekick as part of the Agentic Foundational Modelling team, with a focus on model training and inference optimization.

speakers.name: Neb Jovanovic
speakers.title: MLOps Engineer at Isomorphic Labs
speakers.bio: Neb is an MLOps Engineer at Isomorphic Labs, where they build scalable ML infrastructure to accelerate AI-driven drug discovery. They currently focus on developing and refining inference graph frameworks. With a degree in biochemistry and a former career as a teacher, Neb is uniquely passionate about bridging the gap between complex biological workloads and cloud-native systems. When not wrangling YAML, they are usually playing tennis!

speakers.name: Neil Cresswell
speakers.title: Here from Neil, the CEO of Portainer, former CIO of a large ecommerce provider, and former CTO of a Public Cloud Provider.. oh and an ex Consultant..
speakers.bio:
Neil is the CEO of Portainer.io, former CEO of IndonesianCloud, former CIO of NXP New Zealand, Former VMware Consultant, and systems engineer.

Neil has a vast array of experiences, and can talk tech, talk IT management, and is very aware of operational complexities and how to minimise operational risk.

speakers.name: Nikhil Kurup
speakers.title: Seadi Inc, SVP Engineering
speakers.bio: Nikhil Kurup is the SVP of Engineering at Sedai.io, where he leads the development of autonomous cloud management and machine learning tools designed to simplify cloud operations and boost performance. With over 24 years of software development experience, Nikhil previously held data science and engineering roles at companies like H2O.ai and Teradata. He holds a Master’s degree in Information and Data Science from UC Berkeley.

speakers.name: Niki Manoledaki
speakers.title: Staff Software Engineer | CNCF Ambassador
speakers.bio: Niki Manoledaki is a Staff Software Engineer currently on the Platform Engineering team at Grafana Labs where she monitors carbon and cost at scale. She is a cloud sustainability advocate, keynote speaker, and community organizer. Her open source contributions include the CNCF project Kepler and Operational Resilience TAG's Green Reviews subproject. She is a CNCF Ambassador and Green Software Champion.

speakers.name: Nilekh Chaudhari
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at Microsoft
speakers.bio: Nilekh is a Software Engineer at Microsoft specializing in Kubernetes. He has contributed to key upstream Kubernetes areas via SIG Auth and SIG API Machinery, the Secrets Store CSI Driver ecosystem (driver, sync controller, Azure provider), and the Gatekeeper Library. Nilekh is currently an active contributor to Istio.

speakers.name: Nili Guy
speakers.title: IBM Research Manager
speakers.bio: Nili is a Research Manager and Senior Technical Staff Member at IBM Research, co-creator of llm-d, and an expert in distributed inference and Kubernetes-native AI systems. She has led key open-source and productized inference initiatives across IBM’s AI platforms.

speakers.name: Nina Polshakova
speakers.title: Member of Technical Staff
speakers.bio: Nina is a software engineer working on AI Gateway inference projects. She contributes to open source projects, including Kubernetes, Istio, kagent, agentgateway, and kgateway. A CNCF Ambassador and former Kubernetes v1.33 Release Lead, she’s also a member of the Cloud Native AI Working Group and has co-authored papers on AI security. She enjoys exploring new open source projects and building AI agents—ideally so they can do her job for her. 🤖

speakers.name: Ning Liao
speakers.title: Director of Engineering, Google
speakers.bio: Ning Liao is a Director of Engineering at Google, leading strategy and execution for Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) AI Platform and Distributed Compute Orchestration. Her team builds reliable, efficient, and scalable infrastructure to run the world’s largest AI/ML workloads at a massive scale, while collaborating closely with frontier AI labs. Ning brings a strong foundation in large-scale cloud infrastructure and distributed systems from previous engineering roles at AWS and Microsoft.

speakers.name: Nir Rozenbaum
speakers.title: Senior Engineering Lead, NVIDIA
speakers.bio:
Nir is an engineering leader with deep expertise in Kubernetes and Cloud-Native technologies. 
He is a Maintainer of Kubernetes Inference Gateway, Co-Chair of Kubernetes AI Gateway Working Group and a Maintainer of llm-d subprojects. 
With a proven track record in CNCF open source, he drives innovation in AI workloads on Kubernetes and helps shape industry standards for Cloud-Native inference.

speakers.name: Nishtha Jain
speakers.title: Software Engineering Manager at Google Cloud
speakers.bio: Software Engineering Manager at Google Cloud. I own AI/ML storage for kubernetes.

speakers.name: Nitish Kumar
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Argo CD Maintainer
speakers.bio: Nitish is a Software Engineer at Akuity working on the core Argo team. He is a maintainer of the CNCF-graduated project Argo CD and a former Release Team member of the Kubernetes project. Outside of work, Nitish enjoys playing chess and travelling.

speakers.name: Nont Thanonchai W
speakers.title: Kubernetes Engineer, Northmark Compute and Cloud
speakers.bio: Kubernetes Engineer at Northmark Compute and Cloud and an etcd contributor. Previously a senior software engineer at Microsoft and solutions architect at ExxonMobil.

speakers.name: Norwin Schnyder
speakers.title: Senior Cloud Software Engineer, Airlock
speakers.bio: Norwin Schnyder is a Cloud Software Engineer at Airlock and a Lecturer at the Eastern Switzerland University of Applied Sciences and the University of Applied Sciences and Arts Northwestern Switzerland. With over six years of experience in Kubernetes and various contributions to the Gateway API, he focuses on building secure, cloud-native ecosystems by leveraging the power of Kubernetes operators. Outside of his work, Norwin is a passionate sailor and has experience using Helm at sea.

speakers.name: Olivier Bourgeois
speakers.title: Developer Advocate at Google
speakers.bio: Olivier Bourgeois is a Developer Advocate at Google. With almost 10 years of experience developing with Kubernetes, and before that with OpenStack, Olivier has a strong background in cloud and infrastructure technologies. Now, he channels this experience into advocating for the developer community, creating resources, and fostering connections to help users succeed with GKE and Kubernetes. In his spare time, Olivier enjoys spending time in nature and advocating for inclusive urbanism.

speakers.name: Omer Oz
speakers.title: Software Engineer @ Linkedin Compute Infrastructure
speakers.bio: Omer is a software engineer who loves optimizing large systems. In the past he has worked across different parts of the ML Infra stack and now he works on Compute Infra at LinkedIn, helping run one of the largest Kubernetes installations in the world — +500k bare-metal machines. In his spare time, he loves testing and contributing to open source projects.

speakers.name: Omisha Gupta
speakers.title: AWS, Solutions Architect
speakers.bio: Hi, I'm Omisha, Solutions Architect at AWS. With a strong background in DevOps, I've been at the forefront of scaling and innovating digital solutions. My experience has empowered companies to achieve tenfold growth by leveraging AWS's cutting-edge technologies and Kubernetes. I thrive on helping businesses unlock their potential through robust, secure, and efficient cloud architectures.

speakers.name: Omri Cohen
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer, NVIDIA
speakers.bio: Omri Cohen is a Sr. Software Engineer at NVIDIA. He has been developing the recently open-sourced KAI scheduler and previously the Run:ai scheduler for the past 3 years.

speakers.name: Orlin Vasilev
speakers.title: Principal Open Source Technology Advocate
speakers.bio: Orlin Vasilev is  Open Source and Cloud Native Technology Advocate at SAP. Community Manager for Project Harbor and Project K3s as part of the Cloud Native team. Second term CNCF Ambassador and driving the biggest Meetup Group in Bulgaria and Kubernetes Community Days Sofia organizer.. KubeCon CfP review board member and co-chair for Track 101 and Community.  Previously SysAdmin/Dev/SRE/System engineering roles for over 15 years! Located in Bulgaria, Europe! Father of two - a girl and a boy!

speakers.name: Oscar Castillo
speakers.title: DevOps Engineer
speakers.bio: IT Engineer with 14 years of experience, evolving from Security Architecture to Cloud and Infrastructure Engineering. Speaker at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon, sharing practical insights on cloud-native technologies and platform engineering. Currently working in DevOps and transitioning into Platform Engineering, focused on automation, CI/CD, Kubernetes, containers, and Infrastructure as Code to build scalable, secure, and resilient platforms.

speakers.name: Pablo Fredrikson
speakers.title: Principal SRE at Bitso & YouTuber
speakers.bio: Principal SRE at Bitso and CNCF Ambassador. Working in the field since 2006, working with containers and Kubernetes in production since 2018. Content creator in YouTube and passionate about Open Source.

speakers.name: Paco Xu
speakers.title: DaoCloud, Lead of open source team.
speakers.bio:
Paco is a member of Kubernetes Steering Committee, and co-chair of KubeCon+CloudNativeCon China 2024.

Paco is a kubeadm maintainer and an active kubernetes contributor. His interest includes SIG-Node, LTS and CoreDNS.

He is the leader of the open-source team in DaoCloud. He organized KCD Chengdu 2022 and KCS China 2023, and speaked in KCD Shanghai, KubeCon EU 2023 & 2024 & 2025, and KubeCon China 2021, 2023, 2024 & 2025. He is also LFAPAC Evangelist.

speakers.name: Padma Aradhyula
speakers.title: Solving the planet-scale infrastructure bottlenecks that data and AI leave behind.
speakers.bio: Padma Aradhyula is a Senior Director of Software Engineering at Salesforce and a former lead for Google Dataproc’s compute fabric. Specializing in distributed systems at "planet-scale" , Padma focuses on shifting the AI and big data bottleneck from model architecture to cloud infrastructure efficiency. At Salesforce, her team manages millions of daily Spark applications on Kubernetes and working on continuous optimizations to handle the scale, reliability and price-performance of the workloads.

speakers.name: Parth Arora
speakers.title: IBM/Red Hat, Software Engineer
speakers.bio:
I am Parth Arora, a software developer specializing in distributed storage systems.
As a developer, I have extensive experience working with Rook, a cloud-native storage orchestrator that enables storage systems like Ceph to be run as a service on Kubernetes. I have contributed to the development of Rook and have worked on projects involving Ceph and other distributed storage systems.

speakers.name: Pavan Madduri
speakers.title: W.W.Grainger, Inc Senior Cloud Platform Engineer
speakers.bio: Senior Cloud Platform Engineer at W.W. Grainger, CNCF Golden Kubestronaut, and IEEE Senior Member. I build GPU autoscaling and zero-trust infrastructure for AI workloads on Kubernetes. Creator of keda-gpu-scaler, an open-source KEDA External Scaler for GPU-aware inference scaling. Active contributor to Volcano (GPU NUMA topology) and Dragonfly (AI model distribution). I write about cloud-native AI infrastructure for CNCF.io, VKTR, and PlatformEngineering.com.

speakers.name: Pavani Panakanti
speakers.title: AWS, Software Engineer at EKS
speakers.bio: Pavani is a Software Development Engineer on the AWS EKS Networking team, focused on high-performance networking for AI/HPC workloads on Kubernetes. She works on EFA, RoCEv2, and RDMA integration in EKS, and contributes to the upstream DRANET project (kubernetes-sigs/dranet). Her work spans Dynamic Resource Allocation, eBPF-based network policy enforcement, and accelerator-network topology alignment for distributed training. GitHub: @Pavani-Panakanti

speakers.name: PePe Amengual
speakers.title: Atlantis Maintainer
speakers.bio: I’m a 10x unicorn who fights crimes against Terraform by day and slays manual processes by night. I love open source, devops and helping teams be awesome by empowering them with great tech.

speakers.name: Per Krogslund
speakers.title: Sr Director: Ai, Security, DexEx Programmes @ Docker
speakers.bio:
Former open source startup co-founder and with a history at Zalando and Spotify. Now Director of developer programmes at Docker.

Have a broad background in open source, product, engineering leadership and security.

speakers.name: Peter Hunt
speakers.title: Principal Software Engineer at Red Hat
speakers.bio: Peter Hunt is a Principal Software Engineer working at Red Hat. Passionate about free software, Peter focuses on being a chair for SIG node, maintaining CRI-O, and ~writing~ squashing bugs. Outside of the virtual world, Peter likes collecting floral-printed pants, cooking, and dancing.

speakers.name: Peter Jausovec
speakers.title: Software Architect @ Solo.io
speakers.bio: Peter Jausovec is a software architect at Solo.io with over 18 years of experience in software engineering. A recognized expert in cloud-native technologies, he specializes in Kubernetes, Istio, and AI infrastructure. Peter maintains the kagent project and has been at the forefront of AI and agent projects at Solo.

speakers.name: Phelipe Fabres
speakers.title: Sr. Solutions Architect, GenAI - AWS
speakers.bio: Phelipe Fabres is a Senior Solutions Architect specializing in Generative AI, based in São Paulo, Brazil. He works with high-growth Model Producers AI startups across Latin America, helping founders architect distributed training infrastructure, multi-agent platforms, and GPU-intensive workloads on Kubernetes. His focus areas include VLM fine-tuning at scale, multi-cluster GPU orchestration with CNCF projects, and cloud-native AI inference.

speakers.name: Phil Henderson
speakers.title: Customer Success Engineer - Buoyant
speakers.bio: Accomplished IT professional with 13+ years DevOps experience as a Solutions Architect, Site Reliability Engineer, and SysAdmin. Expertise leading cross-functional teams, optimizing CI/CD pipelines, and enhancing/enforcing security protocols. Adept at driving and implementing technological advancements and efficient workflows to meet organizational goals and improve overall productivity.

speakers.name: Philip Conrad
speakers.title: OPA Maintainer
speakers.bio: Philip Conrad is a Software Engineer at Apple, based out of Columbia, South Carolina. He is a maintainer for the Open Policy Agent and works on tools, frameworks, and performance optimizations for the project. Outside of work, he enjoys board games and bouldering.

speakers.name: Phill Morton
speakers.title: From blueprinting software to blueprinting the cloud – simplifying complexity is my game.
speakers.bio:
Phill is a dedicated software engineer turned platform engineer, with a strong passion for automating processes and enabling team success. 
With extensive experience in app modernization, cloud engineering, performance tuning, and observability. Phill brings a wealth of knowledge to the table. 
Throughout their career, Phill has been committed to demystifying complex processes, making them more accessible for team members, and fostering an environment where innovation and collaboration thrive.

speakers.name: Phong Nguyen
speakers.title: Meta - Production Engineer
speakers.bio: Phong is a Production Engineer at Meta, bridging Meta’s production stack with public cloud and the wider cloud-native world. He ships platforms for everything from standard services to GPU workloads, then grabs the pager when things catch fire. And yes - when the smoke clears, he’s yapping about what worked so you don’t repeat the pain.

speakers.name: Piotr Prokop PL
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA
speakers.bio: Piotr is a Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA. He works on running high performance workloads powered by Kubernetes for NVIDIA products.

speakers.name: Prakash Narayanasamy
speakers.title: Senior Staff Engineer, Nutanix
speakers.bio:
Software engineer with over 25 years of experience designing, developing, and scaling
distributed systems for software-defined data centers, virtualization, and cloud-native data
management.

speakers.name: Pritesh Kiri
speakers.title: DevRel Engineer at Harness | Community Manager at LitmusChaos | Organizer at Reactplay
speakers.bio:
Pritesh is the DevRel Engineer at Harness and community manager and maintainer of the LitmusChaos Community. He is also the Head of Community at ReactPlay, leading the ReactPlay Bangalore chapter. He has a strong background as a Developer Advocate, leading tech communities and fostering open-source contributions.
Pritesh organizes workshops and meetups and creates video/blog content on MCP, Agents, and AI.

speakers.name: Prithvi Raj
speakers.title: Senior Community Manager & Developer Advocate at Mirantis
speakers.bio:
Prithvi Raj is a Senior Community Manager & Developer Advocate at Mirantis working with the OSPO. He is a CNCF Ambassador with 6+ years of experience who helped scale a CNCF incubating project and runs the CNCG Platform Engineering Meetup group. He is currently leading the community efforts for the k0s project, k0rdent, OpenSDN.

He is a co-organizer to KCD Bengaluru, and previously did Chaos Carnival, LitmusChaosCon, KCD Chennai.
He was previously at Harness, ChaosNative, and MayaData.

speakers.name: Priya Namasivayam
speakers.title: EarnIn, Staff Platform Engineer
speakers.bio: Priya Namasivayam is a Staff Platform Engineer at EarnIn, building cloud-native infrastructure at scale. She specializes in Kubernetes, service meshes, and GitOps delivery, and led EarnIn's migration from AWS App Mesh to Linkerd—improving security, reliability, and developer experience. She champions treating infrastructure like application code, gating Flux-driven changes with in-cluster validation via Testkube, and sharing patterns teams can adopt in production.

speakers.name: Priyanka Saggu
speakers.title: Kubernetes Integration Engineer, SUSE
speakers.bio:
Priyanka Saggu is a Kubernetes Engineer at SUSE and a long-time contributor to Kubernetes across SIG ContribEx, Release, Node, and Testing.

She served on Kubernetes Release Teams from v1.23–v1.31, including as Release Lead for v1.29 (Mandala).

She is currently a Technical Lead for SIG ContribEx, a Kubernetes GitHub Admin, and was a co-chair of the first ever CNCF Maintainer Summit.

In SIG Node, she is also a core member of the "Node Readiness Controller" sub-project.

speakers.name: Pronnoy Goswami
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA| Building Distributed Systems That Power The Future | Cloud, AI Ops, Infrastructure | Startup Advisor | Tech Speaker | Ex-Microsoft, McKinsey, PayPal
speakers.bio: Pronnoy Goswami is a Senior Software Engineer at NVIDIA, where he leads next-generation telemetry and logging platforms serving thousands of global customers. Previously at Microsoft Azure, he co-designed the distributed control plane orchestrating container lifecycles at hyperscale. He holds an M.S. in Computer Engineering from Virginia Tech and is an active IEEE technical reviewer and conference speaker on cloud-native observability and distributed systems.

speakers.name: Prschita Prschita
speakers.title: Apple, Engineering Manager
speakers.bio: Prschita is an engineering manager at Apple, leading the Observability Intelligence and Analysis team. Prschita loves to think about and build ML-Driven Observability solutions. She has a background in Observability, Machine Learning, Data Science and Data Engineering.

speakers.name: Qasim Sarfraz
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Microsoft
speakers.bio: Software engineer with 10+ years of experience in cloud-native development and systems engineering. Currently maintaining Inspektor Gadget, a CNCF sandbox project, and actively contributing to open-source projects in the containers and Kubernetes ecosystem. Outside of coding, I’ve spoken at several community events including KCDs, ContainerDays, Cloud Native Rejekts, and KubeCon.

speakers.name: Qianru Lao
speakers.title: Member of Technical Staff, LLM Inference, OpenAI
speakers.bio: Qianru Lao is a Member of Technical Staff on the Inference team at OpenAI, where she works on infrastructure for large-scale model serving. Previously, she contributed to the open-source Delta Lake project at Databricks and worked on distributed storage systems at Alibaba Cloud and infrastructure tooling at Google. She holds degrees in Computational Science and Engineering from Harvard and Computer Science from Sun Yat-sen University.

speakers.name: Rafael Roquetto
speakers.title: OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation Maintainer / Software Technical Leader @ Isovalent (Cisco)
speakers.bio: Maintainer of OpenTelemetry eBPF Instrumentation (OBI), focused on eBPF-based application observability and auto-instrumentation for Kubernetes and cloud-native systems, currently working on Isovalent Tetragon. Software engineer with 20 years of experience spanning embedded Linux, systems programming, and modern C++. Former Qt maintainer and contributor to QtCore, QtMultimedia, Qt Creator, and the QNX integration layer.

speakers.name: Rainie Li
speakers.title: Senior Engineering Manager at Pinterest
speakers.bio: Rainie is a Senior Engineering Manager leading Pinterest’s Data Processing Infrastructure and Big Data Storage Platform teams. She is responsible for the shared compute and storage foundations of Pinterest’s data infrastructure, including K8s/EKS, job submission and routing services, remote shuffle, Iceberg and REST Catalog, Hive Metastore, and related platform capabilities

speakers.name: Raj Bhensadadia
speakers.title: Machine Learning Engineer at Apple
speakers.bio: Raj Bhensadadia, a machine learning engineer with a passion for leveraging ML technologies to enhance monitoring and analysis of large scale systems and ensure robustness and performance of infrastructure and services.

speakers.name: Rajas Kakodkar
speakers.title: Staff Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Rajas is a staff software engineer at Broadcom, where he focuses on low level functions of Kubernetes nodes. He is a tech lead of the CNCF Technical Advisory Group, Workload Foundation and a Kubernetes contributor. He has been co-chairing Cloud Native AI Day, a co-located event at KubeCon since 2024. Rajas has received the CNCF Chop Wood Carry Water Award in 2023 for his contributions and efforts in leading TAG Runtime and has been a co-author of CNCF Whitepaper Cloud Native and AI

speakers.name: Rajith Attapattu
speakers.title: Open Telemetry advocate - CTO @ Randoli
speakers.bio: Rajith Attapattu is a community maintainer of OpenCost and an advocate for OpenTelemetry and open standards. A frequent speaker at CNCF meetups and Kubernetes Community Days, he has also spoken at KubeCon. His current focus is intent-based observability, AIOps, and building intelligent, cost-efficient telemetry pipelines. He previously spent over a decade at Red Hat working on distributed systems.

speakers.name: Randi Armour
speakers.title: Linux Foundation Education, Account Manager
speakers.bio: Randi Armour has spent four years at the Linux Foundation, starting with supporting the growth of open source projects including OpenSSF, Yocto Project, AGL, and CIP. Now an Account Manager in LF Education, she helps private sector, government, and public sector organizations worldwide build skills in cloud native, Linux and embedded systems, AI/ML, and cybersecurity, drawing on firsthand experience across multiple open source communities.

speakers.name: Rani Chowdary Mandepudi
speakers.title: Software Engineer, Arm
speakers.bio: Rani Chowdary Mandepudi is an Arm engineer and open source contributor focused on enabling cloud native workloads on Arm. Rani contributed the upstream Harbor arm64 enablement work, including build/package workflow changes and follow-up dependency fixes, and works with CNCF communities to make Arm support part of normal project release paths.

speakers.name: Rashmi Gottipati
speakers.title: Senior Software Engineer - Red Hat
speakers.bio:
Rashmi is a Senior Software Engineer at Red Hat and a maintainer of the Operator Framework. She has worked across Operator SDK and Operator Lifecycle Manager, helping shape the technologies that enable Kubernetes operators to be built, distributed, and managed at scale.

She focuses on the next generation of Operator Lifecycle Management, building scalable APIs and controllers for Kubernetes extensions. She is passionate about open source, distributed systems, and cloud-native technologies.

speakers.name: Ratnopam Chakrabarti
speakers.title: Sr. Solutions Architect, AWS
speakers.bio: Ratnopam Chakrabarti is a Senior Solutions Architect in AWS's AI/ML organization specializing in AI infrastructure on Kubernetes—spanning AI inference, model fine-tuning, building MLOps pipelines, and running agentic AI systems in production. An active adopter and contributor to CNCF projects, he has previously spoken at events like KCD Texas, Ray Summit and advocates for open-source approaches to running AI infrastructure and agents on Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Ravin Kumar
speakers.title: Research Engineer
speakers.bio: Ravin is a Staff Research Engineer at Google leading specialized small model AI development in specific domains. His research informed from a 10+ year background of generative model development in domain areas such as food supply chain at Sweetgreen, and rocket manufacturing at SpaceX. He is an author of a book focused applied generative modeling, Bayesian Modeling and Computation in Python.

speakers.name: Reese Lee
speakers.title: Senior Developer Relations Engineer, New Relic
speakers.bio: Reese Lee is a Senior Developer Relations Engineer at New Relic focusing on technical enablement via workshops, blog posts, documentation, and more. She is a Maintainer of the OpenTelemetry End User SIG, where she enjoys learning about interesting use cases and the different ways OpenTelemetry has helped teams improve their application and system observability. In her free time, she loves training jiu-jitsu, landscaping & gardening, and watching horror movies.

speakers.name: Regina Voloshin
speakers.title: Argo CD Maintainer, Octopus Deploy
speakers.bio: Regina is a GitOps fan, an ArgoCD maintainer and a CNCF Ambassador.

speakers.name: Rey Lejano
speakers.title: Solutions Architect @ Red Hat, CNCF Ambassador, K8s SIG Docs co-chair, SIG Security subproject lead, K8s v1.23 release lead, DevOps Institute Ambassador
speakers.bio: Rey Lejano is a Solutions Architect at Red Hat and is the co-chair of Kubernetes SIG Docs. He contributes to Kubernetes SIG Security, Release, & Contributor Experience. He is a member of seven Kubernetes Release Teams including serving as the 1.23 Release Lead and 1.25 Emeritus Adviser. Rey leads the Kubernetes SIG Security Third-Party Security Audit subproject and helped release the last security audit in April 2023. Rey is a CNCF Ambassador and DevOps Institute Ambassador.

speakers.name: Reza Jelveh
speakers.title: Solutions Engineer @ Dynamia.ai / HAMi
speakers.bio: Reza Jelveh is a solutions engineer at HAMi (project-hami.io), focusing on the mechanics, constraints, and resource allocation of AI workloads on Kubernetes.

speakers.name: Rian Bogle
speakers.title: Principal Architect at Agility Robotics
speakers.bio: Rian Bogle is Principal Architect at Agility Robotics, where he's building Kubernetes-based platforms to reliably manage fleets of humanoid robots at the edge. He's passionate about making distributed systems work in environments that are anything but predictable — where the "nodes" walk, fall, and get back up. Outside of work, he geeks out on cloud networking, robot identity, and whatever edge case the robots throw at him next.

speakers.name: Ricardo Aravena
speakers.title: AI Infrastructure Lead
speakers.bio:
Ricardo is a Cloud Native AI Lead. He's an open-source enthusiast, currently serving on the CNCF TOC. He has also co-chaired the CNCF TAG-Runtime. Recently, he led the publication of the Cloud Native AI Whitepaper and is currently helping with various initiatives within the Cloud Native AI and PyTorch ecosystem, including the PyTorch Technical Advisory Council (TAC).

He has a diverse professional background spanning over 25 years in tech and software engineering at both large companies.

speakers.name: Ricardo Katz
speakers.title: Software Engineer - Red Hat
speakers.bio: Engineer on Openshift Ingress, Gateway & DNS area at Red Hat. Previously was the tech lead for the Brazilian Government Cloud and Platform infrastructure, being one of the persons responsible for implementing some of the first Kubernetes clusters in Brazil, clusters today that run some of the most mission-critical services for the citizens, and also tech lead of platform for Data Services Manager at VMware.

speakers.name: Ricardo Rocha
speakers.title: Computing Engineer
speakers.bio: Ricardo leads the Platform Infrastructure team at CERN with a strong focus on cloud native deployments and machine learning. He has led for several years the internal effort to transition services and workloads to use cloud native technologies, as well as dissemination and training efforts. Ricardo got CERN to join the CNCF and is a lead of the CNCF Research User Group. Prior to this work Ricardo helped develop the grid computing infrastructure serving the Large Hadron Collider (LHC).

speakers.name: Richard Liaw
speakers.title: Ray Lead at Anyscale
speakers.bio: Co-author of Ray; current Ray lead at Anyscale. Previously PhD at UC Berkeley.

speakers.name: Rishabh Wason
speakers.title: Salesforce/Heroku, Lead Software Engineer
speakers.bio: Rishabh Wason is a Lead Software Engineer at Salesforce/Heroku, where he develops and operates the Control Plane for Fir, Heroku's next-generation Kubernetes-based platform. With eight years in platform engineering, he works on the orchestration layer that connects customers to the compute resources running their applications. He collaborates across Heroku to build scalable, reliable, and secure control plane systems while helping to replatform Heroku onto a unified Kubernetes foundation.

speakers.name: Rishi Mody
speakers.title: Senior Product Manager, AKS
speakers.bio: Rishi is a Product Manager for Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS), focused on hybrid and edge environments and helping organizations run and manage AKS consistently wherever their workloads need to operate. He leads the product efforts for the recently released AKS on bare metal and works closely with engineering teams, customers, and field organizations to simplify the AKS experience and deliver a consistent Kubernetes platform across environments.

speakers.name: Rita Zhang
speakers.title: Principal software engineer, Kubernetes AI Conformance program chair and sig-auth chair
speakers.bio: Rita Zhang is a Principal software engineer at CoreWeave, based in San Francisco bay area. She works on the inference platform powering the serverless and dedicated inference products. She is a Kubernetes sig-auth chair, a Kubernetes AI Conformance program chair, and a maintainer of the Open policy agent Gatekeeper project. Rita is passionate about open source and running distributed workloads at scale.

speakers.name: Roaa Sakr
speakers.title: Principle Software Engineering Manager - Microsoft
speakers.bio: Roaa Sakr is a Principal Software Engineering Manager at Microsoft leading Azure Linux container runtime innovation. She drives secure, high-performance pod sandboxing with Kata Containers and virtualization-based isolation, powering production workloads at scale. An active open-source contributor and former maintainer of CNCF Akri project, she is passionate about advancing collaboration across the cloud-native ecosystem to deliver production-ready, scalable solutions

speakers.name: Robin Deaconu
speakers.title: Software Engineer at Isomorphic Labs
speakers.bio: Robin is a software engineer on the inference team at Isomorphic Labs, building the distributed systems that power AI-driven drug discovery at scale.

speakers.name: Roger Coll
speakers.title: Grafana Labs, Senior Software Engineer
speakers.bio: I am a passionate Unix-like systems enthusiast with an even greater love for open source. As an OpenTelemetry and observability advocate, I strive to promote the importance of comprehensive monitoring and performance insights. When I'm not immersed in technology, you'll find me exploring the great outdoors as an avid mountain hiker.

speakers.name: Rohan Sood
speakers.title: Building Resilient Systems and Scalable Platforms
speakers.bio: Rohan first explored mechanical systems at Berkeley before a fascination with robotics and ML prompted a pivot. He dove into academic research on how machines make sense of the world, exploring SLAM, decision theory, and information theory. After starting his career building machine learning infrastructure, he now works on a similar problem at a different scale: ensuring large cloud infrastructure stacks can make sense of—and survive—the chaos of production.
